It may also be joined (muttaṣil), excepted from the object in يقربكم. It may also be parsed as a mubtadaʾ, with what follows as the khabar. The clause آمن is the ṣila; عمل is conjoined to آمن; صالحا is a mafʿūl bihi, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. righteous work.
(فَأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ جَزاءُ الضِّعْفِ بِما عَمِلُوا): the fāʾ is linking, because of the sense of condition in the relative noun. أولئك is a demonstrative and a mubtadaʾ; the reference is to من, and the plural is in view of its meaning, just as the singular of the two verbs is in view of its wording. لهم is a fronted khabar and جزاء الضعف a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك. The meaning of جزاء الضعف is that their single good deed is multiplied tenfold for them. The annexation is either the annexation of the maṣdar to its object, or the annexation of the qualified noun to its adjective; the meaning on the first is that Allah recompenses them with the multiple, and on the second: they have the multiplied recompense. بما is attached to جزاء; ما is relative or maṣdarī.
(وَهُمْ فِي الْغُرُفاتِ آمِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ; في الغرفات is a ḥāl or is attached to آمنون; آمنون is their khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم» (the verse) there is iltifāt (shift) from the third person to direct address. The secret of it is emphasis in establishing the statement: that what you rejoice and delight in — the abundance of children and wealth — will not avail you in the slightest, nor bring you near to Us so long as you persist in your present state, indulging in answering the calls of error and misguidance. In this there is an implicit indication of spending wealth in the way of Allah and in the avenues of good, and of educating children and preparing them for what will set right their religion and their worldly life. Al-zulfā is nearness (al-qurbā), and al-zulfa is a drawing near (al-qurba).

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلاَّمِ الغَيْبِ﴾: he said: I saw it in the copy of the Qurʾān of ʿAbdullāh as (عَلاَّمِ), according to the reading of his companions. ʿĀṣim read it (عَالِم الغَيْب) in the genitive, as a description of Allah. The people of the Ḥijāz read (عالِمُ الغَيْبِ) in the nominative as a fresh start (iʾtināf), since words intervene between the two; as He said ﴿رَبِّ السمواتِ والأرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُما الرحمنُ﴾ and made it nominative, while the noun before it is genitive. All are correct.
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ﴾ and ﴿يَعْزِبُ﴾ are two dialectal forms, and both have been read. The kasra is dearer to me.

farraa:5-5.t: His saying ﴿عَذَابٌ مِّن رِّجْزٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾: the readers read it in the genitive. Had it been made a naʿt (adjective) of العذاب and put in the nominative, it would have been permissible; as the readers read ﴿عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُنْدُسٍ خُضْرٍ﴾ and ﴿خُضْرٌ﴾, and read ﴿فى لَوْح محفوظٍ﴾ [qualifying] the Tablet, and ﴿محفوظٌ﴾ [qualifying] the Qurʾān. All are correct.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ﴾: (يرى) is in the position of an accusative [subjunctive]. Its meaning is: that He may recompense those … and that those … may see (he recited the verse). If you wish, you begin it afresh and make it nominative [indicative], and the meaning is a fresh start, not referred back to كَيْ.
His saying ﴿وَيَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْعِلْمَ﴾: you make (العلم) accusative because it comes out of [a verb] whose agent is not named, and you make ﴿الذينَ﴾ nominative through (يرى). Its meaning is only: and those who were given the Torah see — ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his companions among the Muslims of the People of the Book. His saying ﴿هُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾: (هو) is a ʿimād (support pronoun) [Translator's note: the Kufan term for what the Basrans call the ḍamīr al-faṣl, the separating pronoun] for الذى. You make ﴿الحقَّ﴾ accusative when you make it a ʿimād. Had you made ﴿الحقّ﴾ nominative, making (هو) a noun [i.e. mubtadaʾ (subject)], it would have been correct. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
ليت الشباب هو الرجِيعُ عَلَى الفتى * والشيبَ كان هو البَدِئ الأوّلُ
(Would that youth were what returns to a young man, and grey hair had been what came first.)
He used the nominative with (كان) and the accusative with (ليت). The accusative is permissible with every [noun having] alif and lām, and with "afʿal minka" (more … than you) and its kind. It is also permissible with nouns that are by their nature definite [i.e. proper names], except that the nominative is more common with [such] names. You say كان عبدُالله هو أخوك (ʿAbdullāh was your brother) more often than كان عبدالله هو أخاك. Al-Farrāʾ said: he allows this, and no other grammarian allows it. [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently a transmitter's remark that al-Farrāʾ alone allows the accusative here.] And [in] كان أبو محمّد هو زيدٌ, the speech of the Arabs is the nominative. They preferred the nominative with names only because the alif and lām were introduced / 151 a [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] as a support for that in which they occur, just as (هو) was introduced as a support for the noun before it. So when they do not find alif and lām in the noun after it, they choose the nominative and treat it like the indefinite; for they say nothing but كانَ عبدالله هو قائم. They allowed the accusative only in أفضل منك (better than you) and its kind, because there is no way to introduce the alif and lām into it, so they allowed their meaning to take effect even though they do not appear, since it is not possible to make them appear. As for قائم, you are able to put the alif and lām on it, so when you do not bring them, they make هو before it a noun, not a ʿimād, since the verbal word [i.e. the participle] has not been supported with alif and lām. The poet said:
أجِدَّك لَنْ تزال نجِىَّ هَمٍّ * تبيتُ الليلَ أنت له ضجيع
(Truly, will you never cease to be the confidant of care, spending the night as its bedfellow?)

farraa:7-8.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ﴾: the Arabs assimilate the lām into the nūn when the lām is quiescent and the nūn is vowelled. That is because it is close to it in point of articulation. It is frequent in recitation. They do not do that with a lām that is sometimes vowelled, such as ادخل and قل, because (قل) [i.e. the verb يقول] used to take the nominative and the accusative, and the jussive enters upon it; whereas هل, بل and أَجَلْ are always quiescent (majzūm), so when they are assimilated they are likened to His saying ﴿النار﴾, when the lām of النار is assimilated into its nūn. Likewise His saying ﴿فَهَلْ تَرَى لَهُمْ مِنْ بَاقِيَةٍ﴾: you assimilate the lām into the tāʾ in بل, هل and أَجَلْ, and you do not assimilate in a lām that is sometimes vowelled. Pronouncing them clearly (iẓhār) is permissible, because the lām is not joined to what follows it as the lām of النار and the like is joined. I have come to choose ﴿هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ﴾ and ﴿بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ﴾ with clear pronunciation only because the recitation of the non-native-born (muwalladūn) is something crafted; they did not take it from the instinct of the Bedouin, they took it by craft. For the Bedouin it is permissible, given the light and heavy speech that runs on his tongue. If I were to make recitation conform by analogy to what is light on the tongues of the Arabs, so that they lighten or assimilate, I would lighten His saying ﴿قُلْ أَىُّ شَىْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً﴾ and say أَيْشٍ أكبرُ شهادة, which is the speech of the Arabs. But recitation is not on that basis [Translator's note: the source has فيلس, apparently for فليس]; recitation is on fullness and giving each sound its due; and because the particle is not joined like the alif and lām: do you not see that you do not pause on the alif and lām [apart] from the word in which they are? For that reason I did not pronounce the lām clearly before the tāʾ and the like. [Translator's note: so in the source; this appears to contradict his stated preference for clear pronunciation just above.] Likewise His saying ﴿اتَّخَذْتُم﴾ and ﴿عُذْتُ بِرَبِّى وَرَبِّكُمْ﴾: you may pronounce clearly or assimilate. Assimilation is dearer to me, because it is joined to a letter before which one cannot pause. As for His saying ﴿بَلْ رَانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, the lām enters very strongly into the rāʾ, and it is heavy on the tongue to pronounce it clearly, so it is assimilated. Do likewise with all assimilation: whatever is heavy on the tongue to pronounce clearly, assimilate; and whatever is easy for you to pronounce clearly, pronounce clearly and do not assimilate.

His saying: ﴿لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ ﴿أَفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾: this alif is interrogative, so it is a disjunctive alif (maqṭūʿa) both in pause and in continuation, because it is the alif of interrogation; the alif after it fell away because it is light and redundant, falling away in connected speech. Likewise His saying ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ﴾ and His saying ﴿أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ﴾ — Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm recited the verse — and His saying ﴿أَصْطَفَى البَنَاتِ عَلَى البَنِينَ﴾. It is not permissible to give the alif a kasra here, because the interrogation would be lost. If you say: why, when two alifs come together, did you not lengthen, as He said ﴿آلذكرين﴾ and ﴿آلآنَ﴾? I say: the alif was lengthened in الآن and the like only because its alif had a fatḥa; had you dropped it, you would find no / 151 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] difference between interrogative and declarative, so the lengthening of the alif was made a distinction between interrogative and declarative. In His saying ﴿أَفْتَرَىٰ﴾ its alif had a kasra and the interrogative alif a fatḥa, so they were distinct and had no need to lengthen the alif.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَىٰ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾: He says: do they not know that wherever they are, they see before them of the earth and the sky the like of what is behind them, and that they cannot get out of them? So how do they feel safe from Our making the earth swallow them, or dropping upon them a punishment from the sky?

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ وَٱلطَّيْرَ﴾: the readers who are known agree on doubling ﴿أَوِّبِي﴾, and its meaning is: glorify [Allah]. Some read (أُوبِى مَعَهُ), from آب يؤوب, i.e. go about with him. ﴿وَٱلطَّيْرَ﴾ is accusative in two ways. One is that you make it accusative by the verb, through His saying ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ مِنَّا فَضْلاً﴾: and We subjected the birds to him. It is then like your saying أطعمته طعاماً وماء (I fed him food and water), meaning: and I gave him water to drink; that is permissible. The other way is by the vocative, because when you say يا عمرو والصَلْت أقبِلا (O ʿAmr and al-Ṣalt, come forward), you make الصلت accusative, because it can only be called with يا أيُّها, so when that is missing, it is as though diverted from its proper path, and it is made accusative. It may also be nominative by following what precedes it. And it may be nominative on [the meaning]: glorify, you and the birds. One of the Arabs recited to me, regarding the vocative when it is made accusative for lack of يا أيُّها:
أَلا يَا عَمْرُو وَالضحّاكَ سِيَرَا * فقد جَاوزتُمَا خَمرَ الطريقِ
(O ʿAmr, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, travel on, for you two have passed the cover of the road.)
al-khamar: whatever conceals you, of trees and other things. (It is permissible) for (الضحّاك) to be accusative or nominative. Another said:
* يا طلحةُ الكاملُ وابن الكَامل *
(O Ṭalḥa, the perfect one and son of the perfect one.)
The naʿt (adjective) runs on the vocative word just as the conjoined does: it is made accusative or nominative. Do you not see that you say إن أخاكَ قائِم وزيد (your brother is standing, and Zayd) and إن أخاك قائم [و] زيدا, so the conjoined after the predicate with إنّ is treated like the naʿt after the predicate?
His saying: ﴿وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلْحَدِيدَ﴾: iron was made to flow for him, so he would work it as he wished, as one works clay.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿أَنِ ٱعْمَلْ سَابِغَاتٍ﴾: coats of mail; ﴿وَقَدِّرْ فِي ٱلسَّرْدِ﴾: He says: do not make the rivet of the coat of mail thin, so that it is loose, nor thick, so that it breaks the rings.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ ٱلرِّيحَ﴾ is accusative on [the meaning]: and We subjected the wind to Solomon. It is accusative in [Sūrat] al-Anbiyāʾ: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ ٱلرِّيحَ عاصِفَةً﴾; He implied "and We subjected" — and Allah knows best. ʿĀṣim — as far as I know — read it nominative (وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ ٱلرِّيحُ), since the subjecting does not appear overtly. One of the Arabs recited to me:
ورأيتُم لمُجَاشعٍ نَعَماً * وبنى أبيه جَامِلٌ رُغُب
(You saw that Mujāshiʿ has livestock, and his father's sons a great, greedy herd of camels.)
He means: and you saw that his father's sons have …; since the verb did not appear, it was made nominative through the lām.
His saying: ﴿غُدُوُّهَا شَهْرٌ وَرَوَاحُهَا شَهْرٌ﴾: He says: its morning journey until midday was a month's travel, and its evening journey likewise.
His saying: ﴿وَأَسَلْنَا لَهُ عَيْنَ ٱلْقِطْرِ﴾ is like ﴿وألَنَّا لَهُ الحَدِيدَ﴾. Al-qiṭr: copper.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَارِيبَ وَتَمَاثِيلَ﴾: it is mentioned that these were images of the angels and the prophets, which were depicted in the places of worship so that people would see them and increase in worship. Al-maḥārīb: places of worship.
His saying: ﴿وَجِفَانٍ﴾: large bowls; (كالجَوابِ): [like] the troughs for camels; (وَقُدُورٍ رَّاسِيَاتٍ): He says: huge, not taken down from their places.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿تَأْكُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُ﴾: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash gave it a hamza. It is the large staff that a herdsman carries; taken from نسأت البعير: I drove the camel on to increase its pace; as one says نسأت اللبَن when you pour water onto the milk, and that is al-nasīʾ; and نُسِئت المرأَة when a woman has become pregnant; and نَسَأَ اللهُ فى / 152 a [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] أجلك, i.e. may Allah extend it. The people of the Ḥijāz did not give it a hamza, nor did al-Ḥasan.
Perhaps they intended the dialect of Quraysh, for they drop the hamza. Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī claimed to me that he asked Abū ʿAmr about it, (مِنْسَاتَهُ) without hamza, and Abū ʿAmr said: because I do not know it, I dropped its hamza. Had it come in recitation as مِن ساتِهِ, you would make (سَاة) one word and put it in the genitive with مِن. Al-Farrāʾ said: likewise Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: it eats from his staff. The Arabs call the tip of the bow al-siya, so it could be from that; it may take fatḥa or kasra — meaning on the sīn — as one says إِنّ به لضِعَةً and ضَعَة (he has lowliness), and قِحَة and قَحَة, from al-waqāḥa (impudence). But no one we know of has read it so.
His saying: ﴿دَابَّةُ الأَرْضِ﴾: the termite (al-araḍa).
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا خَرَّ﴾ — Solomon. According to what is mentioned, [the termite] ate the staff, and he fell. People used to think that the devils knew a secret between two people; when he fell, the matter of the jinn became clear to humankind: that they do not know the unseen, and had they known it they would not have gone on working before him while he was dead. (أَنْ) is in the position of a nominative: ﴿تبيَّن﴾ أن لو كانوا ("it became clear that, had they …"). It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: humankind made the jinn clear [to themselves]; the meaning is then: humankind discerned the matter of the jinn, because when the matter of the jinn became clear to humankind, humankind discerned it; and (أَنْ) is then in the position of an accusative through تبيَّنت. If a reader were to read تبّينتِ الجنّ أن لو كانوا, making the verb belong to humankind and implying them in their verb, he would make الجنّ accusative by the verb of humankind, and (أن) would be repeated [as a badal (substitute)] for الجنّ, so you make it accusative. [Translator's note: the source leaves the conditional without an explicit apodosis such as "it would be correct".]

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ لِسَبَإٍ فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ﴾ was read by Yaḥyā as (فى مَسْكَنِهِمْ), and it is an eloquent Yemeni dialectal form. Ḥamza read (مَسْكِنِهِمْ), and the reading of the general readership is (مَسَاكِنِهِمْ), meaning their dwellings. All are correct. Al-Farrāʾ reads with the reading of Yaḥyā.
His saying: ﴿آيَةٌ جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ﴾: the meaning is: on their right hands and their left hands. "The two gardens" is nominative because it is an explanation (tafsīr) of the sign. Had one of the two words been accusative through كان, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿وَٱشْكُرُواْ لَهُ﴾: the speech is cut off here. ﴿بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ﴾: this is a good land, not salt-marsh.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿سَيْلَ ٱلْعَرِمِ﴾: there was a dam that held back the water, with three sluice-gates in it. They would irrigate from that water from the first gate, then the second, then the last, and it would not run out before the water returned in the following year. They were the most comfortable of peoples in their living. When they turned away and denied the messengers, Allah broke the dam upon them, so it flooded their land, and the sand buried their houses, and they were torn utterly apart, until they became a proverb among the Arabs. The Arabs say: تفرقوا أيادِى سَبَا and أيدى سَبَاً (they scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ). The poet said:
عيناً ترى النَّاس إليها نَيْسَبا * من صَادرٍ وواردٍ أيدى سَبَا
(A spring to which you see the people making a beaten track, those leaving and those arriving, scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ.)
They drop its hamza because of how often it runs on their tongues, and some treat سَبا as declinable (yujrūn) and some do not. Whoever does not treat it as declinable takes it to mean the land [Translator's note: the source has البدلة, apparently for البلدة, "the land"]. Whoever treats it as declinable makes Sabaʾ a man or a mountain, and gives it a hamza. In recitation it is mostly with hamza; I know of no one who dropped its hamza. [Someone] recited to me:
الواردونَ وتيم فى ذرى سَبَأ * قد عَضَّ أعناقَهم جِلْدُ الجواميس
(Those who come down to water, and Taym, in the shelter of Sabaʾ — buffalo hide has bitten into their necks.)
His saying ﴿ذَوَاتَيْ أُكُلٍ﴾: al-ukul is pronounced heavy [with two ḍammas]; some of the people of the Ḥijāz pronounced it light. It is read both with annexation and without / 152 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] annexation. As for al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, they pronounced it heavy and did not annex, so they gave it nunation. In the exegesis they mentioned that it is al-barīr, the fruit of the arāk tree. As for al-athl, it is the well-known tree, similar to the tamarisk, except that it is greater in height.
His saying: ﴿وَشَيْءٍ مِّن سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: they mentioned that it is al-samur (acacia); its singular is samura.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهَلْ نُجَٰزِيۤ إِلاَّ ٱلْكَفُورَ﴾: so Yaḥyā read it, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān too. The general readership: (وهَلْ يُجَازَى إلاَّ الكُفُورُ).
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ﴾: the position of (ذَلِكَ) is accusative through ﴿جَزَيناهم﴾.
Someone may say: how is it that He singled out the ungrateful unbeliever for requital, when requital is for the unbeliever, the Muslim and everyone? It is said: جازيناه is equivalent to كافأناه (We paid him back in kind): the evil deed of the unbeliever with its like. As for the believer, he is rewarded (yujzā), because he is given more and favoured; he is not [merely] paid back (yujāzā). جازيت is also said in the sense of جَزَيت, but the meaning in the clearest speech is as I have described to you; do you not see that He said ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ and did not say ﴿جازيناهم﴾? I have heard جازيت in the sense of جَزيت, and it is like عاقبت and عقَبت, the action being from you alone. And (its pattern — he means —) fāʿaltu is [properly] for your doing and being done to [i.e. mutual action].

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَدَّرْنَا فِيهَا ٱلسَّيْرَ﴾: the distance from one town to the next was made half a day; that is His measuring of the journey.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿رَبَّنَا بَاعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا﴾ is the reading of the general readership. It is also read as a statement: ﴿رَبُّنَا بَعّدَ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنا﴾ ("our Lord has made far apart …") and ﴿بَاعَدَ﴾; and it is read as a supplication: ﴿رَبَّنَا بَعِّدْ﴾; and it is read ﴿رَبَّنا بَعُدَ بَيْن أسفارِنا﴾, in which (بَيْنَ) is in the position of a nominative while being accusative [in form]. Whoever makes it nominative treats it like His saying ﴿لقد تقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾: you make الظن accusative because the confirming falls on it. Its meaning is that he said ﴿فَبِعِزّتِكَ لأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ إِلاَّ عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ المُخْلَصِينَ﴾; Allah said: he found his opinion true concerning them, because he said it only by opinion, not by knowledge. It is also read ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَق عليهم إبليسُ ظَنَّه﴾, making الظن accusative on [the meaning]: he was right about them in his opinion. Had you said ولقد صدق عليه إبليسُ ظنُّه, making both إبليس and الظنّ nominative, it would have been correct by repetition [i.e. as badal (substitute)]: his opinion proved true concerning them; as He said ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشهرِ الحرامِ قِتَالٍ فيه﴾, meaning: about fighting in it; and as He said ﴿ثمَّ عَمُوا وصَمُّوا كثيرٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾. And if a reader were to read ولقد صَدَق عليهم إبليسَ ظَنُّه, meaning: his opinion about them proved true to him — as you say صدقك ظنُّك (your opinion proved true to you); opinion is sometimes wrong and sometimes right. [Translator's note: the apodosis of this last conditional is not stated in the source.]

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن سُلْطَانٍ﴾: [no] authority, as a proof by which he leads them astray; but We gave him power over them in order that We might know who believes in the Hereafter.
If someone says: Allah knows their affair with Iblīs being given power and without his being given power — I say: the like of this is frequent in the Qurʾān. Allah said ﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ حَتَّى نَعْلَمَ المُجَاهِدينَ مِنْكُمْ والصّابِرينَ﴾, while He knows the one who strives and the one who is patient without any testing. There are two ways of looking at it. One is that the Arabs, when they speak to an ignorant person in something like this, set him a condition which they attribute to themselves while they know [the answer], and the speech is framed as though for one who does not know. Of that kind is that someone says: "Fire burns firewood," and the ignorant one says: "Rather, firewood burns fire," and the knowledgeable one says: "We will bring firewood and fire in order to know which of them consumes the other." This is a clear way. The other / 153 a [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] way is that you say ﴿لنَبْلُونَّكُمْ حتَّى نَعْلَمَ﴾ means: until We know [it] from you, so it is as though the action were theirs in origin. Similar to it, as something that points you to it, is His saying ﴿وَهُوَ الذى يَبْدَأُ الخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ َهُوَ أهْوَنُ عَلَيْه﴾ — in your view, O unbelievers; though He did not say (عندكم) ("in your view") — he means: (عندكم) is not in the Qurʾān — but that is its meaning. Similar is His saying ﴿ذُقْ إنَّكَ أَنْتَ العزيزُ الكريمُ﴾ — in your own view, since you used to say it in your worldly life. Similar is what Allah said to Jesus: ﴿أَأَنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾, while He knows what [Jesus] says and what he will answer Him with; and Jesus answered Him, knowing that Allah has no need of his answer. So just as it is fitting that He should ask about what He knows and seek an answer from His servant and prophet, so too He sets as a condition from His own action what He knows, so that it is as though, in the view of the ignorant, He does not know.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ﴾, i.e. the intercession of no angel brought near, nor of any prophet, is of use until he is given permission to intercede. It is also said: until he is given permission concerning the one for whom he intercedes, so (مَنْ) is the one interceded for.
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا فُزِّعَ﴾ is the reading of al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and the people of Medina. The reading of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī is (فُرِّغَ), and the reading of Mujāhid is (حَتّى إِذَا فَزَّعَ), making the verb Allah's. As for al-Ḥasan's reading, its meaning is: until, when the terror has been removed from their hearts and they are emptied of it. That is one way. Whoever says فُزِّع or فَزَّع also means: the terror has been removed from them; (عن) indicates that, as you say: قد جُلِّىَ عنك الفزع (the terror has been cleared from you). The Arabs say of a man إنه لمُغَلَّب when he is a victor, and مغَلَّب when he is defeated. Whoever says مغَلَّب of the defeated means: he is always defeated. Whoever says مغلّب of the victor means people's saying [of him]: he is reckoned the loser [though he wins]. Al-mufazzaʿ may be a coward or a brave man: whoever makes him brave says: it is to such as him that terrors are brought down [for relief]; and whoever makes him a coward, that is clear: he means he is frightened by everything.
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾: the meaning of this is that there was an interval (fatra) between our Prophet and Jesus, Allah bless them both and grant them peace. When Gabriel came down to Muḥammad — peace be upon them both — with the revelation, the inhabitants of the heavens thought it was the coming of the Hour. Some of them said: ﴿مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾, and they did not know, but they said: He has spoken the truth. Had ﴿الْحَقّ﴾ been read in the nominative, i.e. "it is the truth", it would have been correct. Whoever makes it accusative makes the saying fall on it: they said, He said the truth.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى﴾: the exegetes said its meaning is: we are surely on guidance and you are in manifest error; the meaning of (أو), in their view, is the meaning of wāw (and). And so it is in meaning; but Arabic is otherwise: (أو) is not equivalent to wāw. Rather it is used for a matter left to choice, as you say: "If you wish, take one dirham or two": he may take one or two, but he may not take three. On the view of one who does not discern Arabic and makes (أو) equivalent to wāw, he could take three, because on their view it is like your saying: take one dirham and two. The meaning of His saying ﴿وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ﴾ is: we are either astray or guided, and you too are astray or guided — while He knows that His Messenger is the guided one and that others are the astray: the astray ones. So you say in ordinary speech to a man: "One of us is surely a liar," and you have called him a liar without uncovering it. This is frequent in the Qurʾān and in the speech of the Arabs: that speech is turned to its best manner when [the truth] is known; as when you say: "By Allah, So-and-so has arrived," while he is lying / 153 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker], and the knowledgeable one says: "Say: if Allah wills," or "Say: as far as I think," so he gives him the lie in a better way than explicit contradiction. It is part of the speech of the Arabs that they say قاتله الله ("may Allah fight him"), then find it ugly and say قاتعه and كاتعه. They say جُوعاً ("hunger [upon him]!") as an imprecation against a man, then find it ugly and say جُوداً, and some say جُوساً. Of this kind is their saying وَيْحك and وَيْسَكَ; it is really ويلْكَ ("woe to you"), except that these are milder than it, in the same way as what has preceded.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿قُل لَّكُم مِّيعَادُ يَوْمٍ﴾: and if it were read ميعادٌ يَوْمٌ [Translator's note: the source does not complete this conditional]. Had it been in the written text (يوماً) with an alif, it would have been permissible, meaning: an appointment on a day.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿لَن نُّؤْمِنَ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَلاَ بِٱلَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾: the Torah. When the People of the Book said, "The description of Muḥammad is in our scripture," the people of Mecca disbelieved in the Qurʾān and in what is "between its hands": what came before it, the Torah.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ مَكْرُ ٱلْلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ﴾: the scheming belongs neither to the night nor to the day; the meaning is only: rather your scheming by night and day. It is also permissible for us to attribute the action to the night and the day, so that they are like agents, because the Arabs say نهارك صَائم (your day is fasting) and ليلك نائم (your night is sleeping): they attribute the action to the night and the day while in meaning it belongs to human beings; as you say نام ليلُكَ (your night slept), and عَزَم الأمر (the matter resolved), when it is only the people who resolved it. This is among the things whose meaning is known, so the Arabs take latitude with it.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿زُلْفَىٰ إِلاَّ مَنْ آمَنَ﴾: (مَنْ) is in the position of an accusative by exception. If you wish, you make the bringing near fall on it, i.e. wealth brings near only whoever is obedient. If you wish, you make it nominative, i.e. it is none but whoever believed.
Similar is ﴿لاَيَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلاَ بَنُونَ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَتَى الله بقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ﴾: if you wish, you make (مَنْ) in the position of an accusative by exception; if you wish, accusative by ينفع falling on it; and if you wish, nominative, saying: it is none but whoever came to Allah with a sound heart.
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلاَ أَوْلاَدُكُمْ بِٱلَّتِي﴾: if you wish, you make (الَّتى) comprise both the wealth and the children, because (الّتى) can apply to children; and since both are plurals, it is fitting for التى to apply to both. Had He said (باللتَينِ) (the two which [fem.]) it would have been a correct form. And had He said باللّذَينِ (the two which [masc.]) — as you say: أَمّا العسكر والإبل فقد أقبلا (as for the army and the camels, they [two] have come). The Arabs have said: مرَّت بنا غَنَمان سُودان (two black flocks of sheep passed us), so he said غَنَمان; had he said غَنَم it would have been permissible. This is evidence for whoever says (بالتى). Had you directed (التى) to the children [Translator's note: the source has الأواد, apparently for الأولاد] and been content with it [i.e. with mention of the wealth] instead of mentioning the children, that would be sound, as Marrār al-Asadī said:
نحن بما عندنا وأنت بمَا * عِندك رَاضٍ والرأىُ مختلفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content, and opinion differs.)
Another said:
إِنى ضمِنت لمن أتَانى مَا جَنَى * وأبى وكان وكنت غير غَدُور
(I have guaranteed whoever came to me [against] what he committed — I and my father; and he was, and I was, not treacherous.)
He did not say غير غَدُورين (not treacherous [dual]). Had He said وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم بالذِينَ, taking it as masculine for the children, it would have been permissible.
His saying: ﴿لَهُمْ جَزَآءُ ٱلضِّعْفِ﴾: had you made it accusative by the nunation in الجزاء, it would have been correct. And if it were said ﴿لَهُمْ جَزَاءُ الضِّعْفُ﴾, and if you said جَزَاءٌ الضِّعْفُ, as He said ﴿بِزِينَةٍ الكَوَاكِبِ﴾ [Translator's note: the source does not complete these conditionals]. ﴿وَهُمْ فِي ٱلْغُرُفَاتِ﴾ and ﴿الغُرْفة﴾ [are both read].

farraa:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ مِّنْ كُتُبٍ يَدْرُسُونَهَا وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ﴾, i.e. on what grounds did they call you a liar, when no scripture and no warner came to them with this?

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبلِهِمْ﴾: and the people of Mecca did not attain a tenth (miʿshār) of those whom We destroyed, in strength of body and wealth. It is also said: they did not attain a tenth of what We gave them [those before] in numbers. Al-miʿshār in both interpretations is a tenth.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُمْ بِوَاحِدَةٍ﴾, i.e. it suffices me from you that a man of you should stand alone, or he and another, and then you reflect: have you ever found Muḥammad lying, or have they seen madness in him? In that is what will make them certain that he is a prophet [Translator's note: the source has بنىٌّ, apparently for نبىٌّ].

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿عَلاَّمُ ٱلْغُيُوبِ﴾: you make (عَلاّم) nominative, and that is the preferred form, because when the naʿt (adjective) comes after the khabar (predicate) with إنّ, the Arabs make it nominative; they say: إن أخاك قائم الظريفُ (your brother, the elegant one, is standing). Had they made it accusative, it would be a valid form. Similar is ﴿إنّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النّارِ﴾: had it been read in the accusative it would have been correct, but the good reading is the nominative.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ﴾: al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read it with hamza, taking it to be from something slow, from نأشت, from al-naʾīsh. The poet said:
* وجئت نئيشا بعد ما فاتك الخبر *
(And you came late, after the news had escaped you.)
Another said:
تمنى نئيشاً أَن يكون أطاعنى * وقد حَدَثت بعد الأمور أمورُ
(He wished, too late, that he had obeyed me, when after events other events had occurred.)
The people of the Ḥijāz and others dropped its hamza, taking it from نُشْته نَوْشا, which is taking hold of something. The two are close, like ذِمْتُ الشىء and ذَأمْته, i.e. I found fault with it. The poet said:
فَهْى تَنُوش الحوض نَوْشاً من عَلاَ * نَوْشاً به تقطع أجواز الفَلاَ
(She reaches at the trough from above, a reaching with which she cuts across the midst of the deserts.)
تناوش القومُ in fighting is when they reach at one another without coming fully close. It may also take a hamza while being from نُشت, because of the ḍamma on the wāw — meaning التناوش — like His saying ﴿وَإِذَا الرُسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ﴾.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ كَـفَرُواْ بِهِ مِن قَـبْلُ وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾: they say he is not a prophet, and Allah has put them far from knowing that, because they have no knowledge; they only speak by conjecture and of the unseen, hoping to establish that he is not a prophet.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The relative noun is a naʿt (adjective) of the Divine Name. The preposition «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause), and the clause «له ما في السماوات» is the ṣila of the relative noun. «ما»: mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «له» is attached to the khabar (predicate). The implied form is: [Praise be] to Allah, Him to whom what is established in the heavens belongs. The clause «وهو الحكيم» is conjoined to the ṣila clause.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «يعلم» is a third khabar (predicate) of the preceding «هو». The clause «وهو الرحيم» is conjoined to the clause «يعلم», and «الغفور» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «بلى»: a particle of answer. His words «وربي»: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; «ربي» is the thing sworn by, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (muqaddar) «أقسم» ("I swear"), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). «عالم»: naʿt (adjective) of «ربي». The clause «لا يعزب عنه مثقال» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ربي». The preposition «في السماوات» is attached to a naʿt of «ذرة». His words «ولا أصغر»: the wāw is a conjunction, «لا» is negating, «أصغر» is a noun conjoined to «مثقال». «إلا» is for restriction. The preposition «في كتاب» is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: except that it is in a Book; the clause is resumptive, meaning: rather, all things are in a Book.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive, «ليجزي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ}. The clause «أولئك لهم مغفرة» is resumptive, and the clause «لهم مغفرة» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «أولئك».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The wāw in «والذين» is resumptive. «معاجزين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «سعوا». The clause «أولئك لهم عذاب» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين», and the clause «لهم عذاب» is the khabar of «أولئك».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «ويرى الذين» is resumptive. His words «الذي أنزل» are the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يرى», and «الحق» is the second object; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). The clause «ويهدي» is conjoined to «الحق», of the type of conjoining clauses to single words, i.e.: they see [it as] the truth and guidance. «الحميد»: naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «ينبئكم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجل». «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the sense of the apodosis, i.e.: you will be resurrected. It is not attached to his words «إنكم لفي خلق جديد», because what comes after «إنَّ» does not govern what precedes it. The conditional clause is parenthetical between the verb and its object. The clause «إنكم لفي خلق» takes the place of the second and third objects of the verb «ينبئكم», and «إن» is given kasra because of the presence of the lām in the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) of «افترى» was dropped when it met the interrogative hamza. «أم» is a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction. The clause «أفترى» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the clause «أم به جنة» is conjoined to the clause «أفترى». The clause «الذين لا يؤمنون» is resumptive, and the preposition «في العذاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «الذين».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The hamza is interrogative and the fāʾ is resumptive. The adverb «بين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). The preposition «من السماء» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the two relative nouns. The conditional clause is resumptive. The second preposition «من السماء» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «كسفا», and the preposition «لكل» is attached to a naʿt of «آية». The clause «إن في ذلك لآية» is resumptive, and the lām is for emphasis.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The preposition «منَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فضلا». The clause «يا جبال» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied speech, the implied form being: our saying; and the implied [word] is a badal (substitute) of «فضلا». His words «والطير»: a noun conjoined to the position of «جبال». His words «معه»: an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl from the yāʾ in «أوِّبي». The clause «وأَلَنَّا» is conjoined to the clause «آتينا».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «أن» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām. «سابغات» is of the type where the described noun is omitted and the adjective kept, i.e.: full-length coats of mail (دروعًا سابغات). «صالحا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «اعملوا» is conjoined to the clause «قَدِّر». The clause «إني بصير» is resumptive, and the preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بصير».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: His words «ولسليمان الريح»: the wāw is resumptive, and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (سخَّرنا, "We subjected"); «الريح» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the implied «سخَّرنا», and the clause «سخَّرنا» is resumptive. The clause «غدوها شهر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الريح». The clause «وأَسَلْنَا» is conjoined to the clause «سخَّرنا», and the clause «ومن الجن من يعمل» is conjoined to the clause «سَخَّرْنا». The preposition «بإذن» is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «يعمل», and the preposition «منهم» is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يَزِغْ». The clause «ومن يَزِغْ» is resumptive, and «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «يعملون» is explicative of the work of the jinn before him. The preposition «من محاريب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما», and the preposition «كالجواب» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «جِفان». «شكرا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e.: perform acts of obedience; good deeds are called gratitude because they are among its kinds. The clause «اعملوا» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied speech, and this speech is resumptive. His words «وقليل»: the wāw is resumptive, «قليل» is a khabar (predicate) placed first and «الشكور» a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later; the clause is resumptive, and the preposition «من عبادي» is attached to a naʿt of «قليل».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «ما دلَّهم» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The clause «تأكل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «دابة الأرض». The second conditional clause is conjoined to the first. His words «أن لو»: «أن» is lightened from the heavy [أنَّ], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن لو ...» is the object of «تبينت» in the sense of "knew". The clause «لو كانوا...» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and the clause «ما لبثوا» is the apodosis of «لو».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «لقد كان» is the response to the oath. The preposition «في مسكنهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آية». «جنتان»: badal (substitute) of «آية». The preposition «عن يمين» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «جنتان». The clause «كلوا» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied, resumptive speech. His words «بلدة»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: this [is]; and «رب»: khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: and the Bestower [is] a Lord. The clause «هذه بلدة» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «فأعرضوا» is resumptive. His words «جنتين»: second object, and the bāʾ entered upon what is given up. «ذواتَيْ»: naʿt (adjective), accusative with the yāʾ. The preposition «من سدر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of «شيء».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: His words «ذلك»: the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «جزى», placed first. «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جزى», i.e.: We recompensed them for their disbelief. The clause «وهل نجازي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «وجعلنا» is conjoined to the clause {جَزَيْنَاهُمْ}. «بينهم»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied second object. «التي»: naʿt (adjective). «قرى»: the first object of «جعلنا». The clause «سيروا» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied speech that is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw, i.e.: saying. «ليالي»: an adverb of time attached to «سيروا», and «آمنين»: ḥāl from the wāw in «سيروا».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «فقالوا» is resumptive. The clause «وظلموا» is conjoined to the clause «قالوا», and the clause «فجعلناهم» is conjoined to the clause «ظلموا». «كل» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The preposition «لكل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آيات».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «ولقد صدَّق عليهم» is resumptive, and the clause «فاتبعوه» is conjoined to the clause «صدَّق». «فريقا»: excepted. The preposition «من المؤمنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فريقا».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «وما كان» is conjoined to the response to the oath. The preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and the preposition «عليهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سلطان». «وسلطان» is the noun of «كان», and «ومن» is redundant (zāʾida). «إلا» is for restriction. «لنعلم»: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive, is attached to the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar of «كان» is attached, i.e.: there was no authority existing for him except so that We might know. The preposition «ممن» is attached to «نعلم» in the sense of "distinguish"; the preposition «منها» is attached to a ḥāl from «شك»; and the preposition «على كل» is attached to «حفيظ».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of the implied second object, i.e.: you claimed them [to be] gods existing besides Allah; the two objects of «زعم» are implied. The clause «لا يملكون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين», i.e.: call them while they possess nothing. The preposition «في السماوات» is attached to a naʿt of «مثقال ذرة». The clause «وما لهم من شرك» is conjoined to the clause «لا يملكون»; «شرك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition «فيهما» is attached to a ḥāl from «شرك». «ظهير» is a mubtadaʾ and «من» is redundant; the preposition «منهم» is attached to a ḥāl from «ظهير».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause «لا تنفع» is conjoined to the clause {لا يَمْلِكُونَ}. «عنده»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الشفاعة». «إلا» is for restriction. The preposition «لمن» is attached to a ḥāl from «الشفاعة». «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), and the clause after it is resumptive. The preposition «عن قلوبهم» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا»: a relative noun, khabar (predicate). «الحق»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied [verb], i.e.: they said: He said the true word. The clause «وهو العلي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «الله»: mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: [is] the Provider. His words «إياكم»: a detached pronoun conjoined to the noun of «إن». The clause «وإنَّا لعلى هدى» is conjoined to the clause (الله الرازق).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «لا تسألون» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl).

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «وهو الفتاح العليم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: His words «أروني»: [from the verb of] sight, transitive to one object before the transfer [to the causative form], and after the transfer it became transitive to two: the yāʾ of the speaker and the relative noun. «شركاء»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun referring back to the relative noun, i.e.: make me see those you attached to Him, as being partners [of mine]. «كلا»: a particle of rebuke and deterrence. The clause «بل هو الله» is resumptive, and «العزيز الحكيم» are multiple predicates (akhbār).

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «وما أرسلناك» is resumptive. «كافة»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) for intensiveness; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern fāʿila, like «العافية». The preposition «للناس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar «كافة». «بشيرا»: ḥāl from the kāf. The clause «ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون» is conjoined to the clause «ما أرسلناك».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «متى»: an interrogative noun, an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). «هذا»: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «إن كنتم صادقين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «لا تستأخرون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ميعاد يوم». «ساعة»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «بين يديه»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). The clause «ولو ترى» is resumptive; the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, i.e.: you would have seen a wonder; and the object of «ترى» is omitted, i.e.: you see the state of the wrongdoers. The clause «الظالمون موقوفون» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). The clause «يرجع بعضهم» is a second khabar (predicate). The adverb «عند» is attached to «موقوفون». The clause «يقول الذين» is resumptive. «أنتم»: mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar is omitted, the implied form being "present" (موجود).

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The adverb «بعد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «صددناكم». «إذ»: an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct), and the clause «جاءكم» is muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «كنتم مجرمين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause that is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) is omitted, its implied form being: we were not criminals; rather... His words «مكر»: fāʿil (agent) of an implied verb, i.e.: your scheming in these two times turned us away. «إذ»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (مكر). The interpreted maṣdar «أن نكفر» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ. The conditional clause «لما رأوا» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause «وأسَرُّوا» is conjoined to the clause «قال الذين». The clause «وجعلنا» is conjoined to the clause «رأوا». The preposition «في أعناق» is attached to the second object of «جعلنا». «ما كانوا»: a relative noun, second object of «يجزون».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The clause «وما أرسلنا» is resumptive; «نذير» is the object of «أرسلنا», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «قال مترفوها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قرية»; what permitted the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) to be indefinite is that a negation precedes it. The preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «كافرون».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «أموالا»: tamyīz (specification). «ما» is a negating particle acting like «ليس», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate). The clause «وما نحن بمعذبين» is conjoined to the clause «نحن أكثر».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «ولكن أكثر» is conjoined to the clause «إن ربي يبسط».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The wāw is resumptive. «ما» is a negating particle acting like «ليس». The preposition «بالتي» is the khabar (predicate), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); it [«التي»] is an adjective of «الأموال» and «الأولاد», because a broken plural of non-rational beings is treated as a feminine singular. «عندنا»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «زلفى». «زلفى»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) synonymous with its governing word. «من»: a relative noun, excepted in a disjoined exception. The clause «فأولئك لهم جزاء» is resumptive. «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the maṣdar «بعملهم» is attached to the maṣdar (جزاء). The clause «لهم جزاء» is the khabar of «أولئك». The clause «وهم آمنون» is conjoined to the clause «لهم جزاء», and the preposition «في الغرفات» is attached to «آمنون».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The wāw is resumptive. «معاجزين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw. The clause «أولئك محضرون» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين». The preposition «في العذاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «محضرون».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The conditional clause «وما أنفقتم» is conjoined to the clause «إن ربي». «ما»: a conditional noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first. The preposition «من شيء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ما». The clause «وهو خير الرازقين» is conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: His words «ويوم»: the wāw is resumptive, and «يوم» is an adverbial noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) «اذْكُر» ("remember"). The clause «يحشرهم» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). «إياكم»: a detached accusative pronoun, object of «يعبدون» placed first. The clause «كانوا» is the khabar (predicate) of the demonstrative.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: «سبحانك»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: we glorify [You], glory be to You. The preposition «من دونهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «ولينا». The clause «كانوا» is resumptive. The clause «أكثرهم مؤمنون» is resumptive, and the preposition «بهم» is attached to the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: His words «فاليوم»: the fāʾ is resumptive, «اليوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يملك». The preposition «لبعض» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نفعا». The clause «ونقول» is conjoined to the clause «لا يملك». The preposition «بها» is attached to «تكذبون».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. «بينات»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آياتنا». The clause «يريد» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجل», and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is the object of «يريد». The preposition «عمَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يصدَّكم». The second clause «وقالوا» is conjoined to the first, and «مفترى» is a naʿt of «إفك». The clause «وقال» is conjoined to the clause «وقالوا». The clause «لما جاءهم» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. «إن» is negating, and «إلا» is for restriction.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The wāw is resumptive. «كتب»: second object of «آتيناهم», and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «يدرسونها» is a naʿt (adjective). The clause «وما أرسلنا» is conjoined to the clause «وما آتيناهم»; «نذير» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «من» is redundant.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «وكذَّب» is conjoined to the preceding resumptive [clause] «وما آتيناهم». The preposition «من قبلهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). «ما»: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). The clause «فكيف كان نكير» is conjoined to the clause «كذَّبوا». «كيف»: an interrogative noun, khabar (predicate) of «كان», and «نكير» is the noun of «كان», nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ, which was dropped for lightness.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تقوموا» is a badal (substitute) of «بواحدة». «مثنى»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw. The clause «ما بصاحبكم من جنة» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of reflection, which carries the sense of knowing and is suspended [from operating] by the negation. «جنة» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition «بصاحبكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «جنة». The clause «إن هو إلا نذير» is resumptive. The preposition «لكم» is attached to «نذير», and likewise the adverb «بين».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: His words «من أجر»: second object of «سأل», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). «ما»: conditional, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «فهو لكم» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The clause «إن أجري إلا على الله» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the clause «وهو على كل شيء شهيد» is conjoined to the clause «إن أجري إلا على الله». The preposition «على كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهيد».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: «يقذف» is made to carry (mudammin) the sense of "decrees" (يقضي), and the preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يقذف». «علام» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «وما يبدئ الباطل» is conjoined to the clause «جاء الحق».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: His words «فبما»: the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and «ما» in his words «فبما» is maṣdar-forming; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate), i.e.: my being guided is by revelation.

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: His words «ولو ترى»: the wāw is resumptive, «لو» is a non-jussive conditional particle, the object of «ترى» is omitted, i.e.: their state, and the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, i.e.: you would have seen a wonder. His words «إذ»: an adverb used in a future context because its occurrence is certain. The clause «فزعوا» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). The clause «فلا فوت» is conjoined to the clause «فزعوا», and the khabar (predicate) of «لا» is implied, i.e.: for them. The clause «وأخذوا» is conjoined to the clause «فزعوا».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: His words «وأنَّى»: the wāw is parenthetical, «أنى» is an interrogative noun, khabar (predicate) placed first, and «التناوش» is the mubtadaʾ (subject). The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (التناوش), and the preposition «من مكان» is attached to the maṣdar (التناوش). The clause «وأنى لهم التناوش» is parenthetical between the ḥāl (circumstantial) clause and the one it describes.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The clause «وقد كفروا به» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in «قالوا», and the clause «ويقذفون» is conjoined to the clause «كفروا».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «وحيل بينهم» is conjoined to the clause {فَزِعُوا}. The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «حيل» is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb, i.e.: the intervening was made to intervene (حِيل الحَوْلُ). «بينهم»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. His words «كما»: the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ما» is maṣdar-forming, i.e.: an intervening was made like Our doing with their kind.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, exalted is He, {يعلم مَا يلج فِي الأَرْض}: يعلم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the name of Allah, exalted be His mention; it may also be a new sentence (mustaʾnaf).

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying {ينبئكم إِذا مزقتم}: the governor of إذا is a verb indicated by the sentence, its implied form being "he informs you of resurrection — or of life, or of being raised — when you have been torn apart". Some allowed the governor to be مزقتم, but that is not good, because إذا is annexed to the clauses and verbs that follow it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf, since it is like part of it, just as one part of a noun does not govern another part. Nor may the governor be ينبئكم, because he is not informing them at that time, so the meaning does not allow it.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {يَا جبال أوبي مَعَه وَالطير}: whoever reads الطير in the accusative conjoins it to the position of الجبال, because it is in the position of the accusative in the sense of the vocative; this is the view of Sībawayh. It is also said that it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). Abū ʿAmr said: it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and We subjected the birds to him". Al-Kisāʾī said: its implied form is "and We gave him the birds", as though it were conjoined to فضل. Al-Aʿraj read it in the nominative, conjoining it to the wording of الجبال. It is also said that it is conjoined to the nominative latent pronoun in أوبي; that is good because معه has separated the two, so it stands in place of the tawkīd (emphasis).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {أَن اعْمَلْ}: أن is explicative (tafsīr) with no grammatical position, meaning أي. It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "for (لأن) 'make'", i.e. "and We softened iron for him for this purpose".

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {غدوها شهر}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), its implied form being "the journey of its morning course is a month's journey", and likewise رواحها شهر. That was needed only because the morning course and the evening course are not themselves the month; they only take place within it.
His saying {وَمن الْجِنّ من يعْمل}: من is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and what precedes it is the khabar. It is also said that من is in the position of the accusative by conjunction to what سخرنا governs, i.e. "and We subjected to him, of the jinn, those who work".
His saying {وَمن يزغ}: من is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; it is conditional, a complete noun, and نذقه is the apodosis (jawāb), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t:
His saying {منسأته}: whoever reads it with an alif (منساته), the origin of the alif is a hamza with fatḥa; but replacement occurred here, whereas the analogical rule is to make the hamza "between a hamza and an alif" (bayna bayna) in lightening. This came by way of replacing the hamza, and it is not taken as a basis for analogy. The hamza is the original.
His saying {تبينت الْجِنّ أَن لَو كَانُوا}: أن is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for الجن, and the implied form is "it became clear to mankind that the jinn, had they…". It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative by omission of the lām.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t:
His saying {آيَة جنتان}: جنتان is a badal (substitute) for آية, which is the ism (noun) of كان. You may also put جنتين in the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), "they are two gardens", and the clause would be in the position of the accusative as an explanation (tafsīr).
His saying {فِي مساكنهم}: whoever reads it in the singular with fatḥa on the kāf (مسكَنهم) makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun), so he did not pluralise it, and brought it according to the analogical rule, because for فَعَل يفعُل the analogical maṣdar comes with fatḥa, as in المقعد, المدخل and المخرج. It is also said that it is a singular noun of place that stands for the plural. Whoever reads the kāf with kasra (مسكِنهم) makes it a noun of place, like المسجد; it is also said that it too is a maṣdar that departs from the rule, like المطلع.
His saying {بَلْدَة}: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is a land", and likewise ورب غفور, i.e. "and this is a forgiving Lord".

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {ذواتي أكل خمط}: whoever annexes الأكل to الخمط makes الأكل the fruit and الخمط the tree, so he annexed the fruit to its tree, as you say "these are dates of palms" and "grapes of vines". It is also said: since it was not good for الخمط to be a naʿt (adjective) of الأكل, because الخمط is the name of a specific tree, and it was not good for it to be a badal (substitute), because it is neither the first nor part of it, while produce and fruit come from trees, it was annexed with the implied sense of من ("of"), like your saying هذا ثوب خز. As for whoever gives it tanwīn, he makes الخمط a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) for الأكل, so that it makes clear that the produce belongs to this tree, which is al-khamṭ, since it could not be an adjective nor a badal; so by it he made clear whose produce, of which tree, it is.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {ذَلِك جزيناهم}: ذلك is in the position of the accusative by جزينا.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {ليَالِي وأياما}: both are adverbs of time for the travelling. الليالي is the plural of ليلة, and it is irregular, as though the original singular were ليلاة; so it was pluralised on something other than the form of its singular, like ملاقح, the plural of ملقحة, though ملقحة is not used, and likewise مشابه, the plural of مشبهة, which is not used.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {وَلَقَد صدق عَلَيْهِم إِبْلِيس ظَنّه}: whoever reads صدق without doubling puts ظنه in the accusative as an adverb, i.e. "he was truthful in his opinion"; by extension (ittisāʿ) you may also put it in the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it is also said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). As for whoever doubles صدّق, ظنه is the object of صدّق. Whoever reads صدق without doubling, with إبليس in the accusative and الظن in the nominative, makes الظن the agent of صدق and puts إبليس in the accusative as the object of صدق, and the implied form is "Iblīs's opinion proved true to Iblīs", as you say ضرب زيدا غلامه, i.e. Zayd's servant struck (him). Whoever reads it without doubling with both in the nominative makes ظنه a badal (substitute) for إبليس, and it is the badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {مَاذَا قَالَ ربكُم}: ما is in the position of the accusative by قال, and ذا is redundant (zāʾida). The evidence for that is His saying, exalted is He, {قَالُوا الْحق}: the answer is accusative by قال, and so must the question be. In ordinary speech the nominative of الحق is permissible, by making ما an interrogative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with ذا in the sense of الذي as its khabar (predicate), and with قال there is an omitted hāʾ, its implied form being "what thing is it that your Lord said?"; then the answer is nominative since the question is nominative. Parallels of this have already passed.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {وَإِنَّا أَو إيَّاكُمْ}: it is conjoined to the ism (noun) of إنّ, and لعلى هدى is the khabar (predicate) of the second, which is إياكم, while the khabar of the first is omitted because the second indicates it; this is the preference of al-Mubarrad. Sībawayh holds that لعلى هدى is the khabar of the first, and the khabar of the second is omitted because the first indicates it. If in ordinary speech you conjoined أو إياكم to the position of the ism of إنّ, you would say أو أنتم, and لعلى هدى would be the khabar of the second and nothing else, with the khabar of the first omitted; there is no disagreement about this, because conjunction to the position of the ism of إنّ can only be after the khabar has passed, so the khabar of the first must be implied before the conjoined word, so that conjunction to the position comes after the khabar has been given.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {إِلَّا كَافَّة}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its meaning is "gathering all people".

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {قل لكم ميعاد يَوْم}: He annexed الميعاد to اليوم by extension. In ordinary speech ميعادٌ يومٌ, both with tanwīn and nominative, is permissible, the second being a badal (substitute) for the first and being the same thing, on the implied form "the time of the appointment is a day". ميعاد is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and لكم is the khabar (predicate). You may also put يوما in the accusative as an adverb, with the hāʾ in عنه referring to the adverb. If you make it refer to الميعاد, you annex يوما to what follows it and say يومِ لا تستأخرون عنه. It is not permissible to annex يوم to what follows it if you make the hāʾ refer to the day, because you would be annexing a thing to itself: the day, annexed to a clause containing a hāʾ which is the day, so you would have annexed the day to the hāʾ while it is the same thing.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t:
His saying {لَوْلَا أَنْتُم}: according to al-Mubarrad nothing other than this is permissible: you bring a nominative pronoun just as the overt noun (after لولا) is nominative. Sībawayh allowed لولاكم, with the pronoun in the position of the genitive, contrary to what the overt noun is; al-Mubarrad rejected it.
[Translator's note: the source reads «تأتي تضمير», evidently for «تأتي بضمير»; translated accordingly.]

mekki-muskil:37-37.t:
His saying {عندنَا زلفى}: زلفى is in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as though He said "a bringing near" (إزلافا); الزلفى is nearness, as though He said "bring you near to Us with a bringing near". According to al-Farrāʾ التي (in بالتي) refers to the wealth and the children. It is also said that it refers to the children specifically, and the khabar (predicate) of the wealth is omitted because the second indicates it, its implied form being "and your wealth is not that which brings you near to Us, nor are your children that which brings you near"; then the first was omitted because the second indicates it.
[Translator's note: the source has «وحذف خاصة وحذف خبر الأمواء», apparently a garbled duplication; «الأمواء» is presumably «الأموال». Translated by its evident sense.]
His saying {إِلَّا من آمن}: من is in the position of the accusative according to al-Zajjāj as a badal (substitute) for the kāf and mīm in تقربكم. This is an error, because the addressee is not substituted for; rather it is accusative by exception. A badal of the absent (third person) for the addressee has come with repetition of the governor, namely His saying, exalted is He, {لقد كَانَ لكم فيهم أُسْوَة حَسَنَة}: then He substituted for the kāf and mīm with the repetition of the preposition, saying لمن كان يرجو.
His saying {فَأُولَئِك لَهُم جَزَاء الضعْف}: جزاء is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك. In ordinary speech جزاءٌ الضعفُ is permissible, with tanwīn on جزاء and الضعف nominative as a badal for جزاء; it is also permissible to drop the tanwīn because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, with الضعف nominative; but nothing of that is read. It is also permissible to put جزاء in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), with الضعف nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and لهم as the khabar, and the clause as the khabar of أولئك.

mekki-muskil:46-46.t:
His saying {أَن تقوموا}: أن is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for واحدة, or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is that you stand". It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative by omission of the lām.
His saying {مثنى وفرادى}: two aḥwāl (circumstantial expressions) from the latent pronoun in تقوموا.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t: His saying {قل إِن رَبِّي يقذف بِالْحَقِّ علام الغيوب}: whoever reads علام in the nominative makes it a naʿt (adjective) of رب according to (its) position, or a badal (substitute) for it, or a badal for the latent pronoun in يقذف. Whoever reads it in the accusative — and that is ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar — makes it a naʿt of رب according to (its) wording, or a badal. The nominative is also permissible as a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, or by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject).

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {التناوش}: it is from ناش ينوش, when one takes hold of something; so its meaning is "how can they take hold of repentance after death" — it is also said: after the resurrection. It has no basis with hamza. Whoever reads it with hamza does so because the wāw took ḍamma after an extra alif, so he turned it into hamza. It is also said that it is from النتيش, which is movement with slowness; on this view its origin is with hamza and nothing else.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿الحمد لله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض﴾: (الحمد): mubtadaʾ (subject); (لله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (الذي): a relative noun, an adjective. (له): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ما): a relative noun, the postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السماوات): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. (وما في الأرض): conjoined to ﴿ما في السماوات﴾; and the clause ﴿له ما في السماوات ...﴾ is the ṣila of (الذي), a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وله الحمد في الآخرة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (له): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (الحمد): postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (في الآخرة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الحمد).
﴿وهو الحكيم الخبير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (هو): mubtadaʾ (subject); (الحكيم): first khabar (predicate); (الخبير): second khabar of ﴿هو﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿يعلم ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها﴾: (يعلم): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو), referring to Allah the Exalted; (ما): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿يلج﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (في الأرض): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يلج﴾; (ما يخرج): conjoined to ﴿ما يلج﴾; (منها): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يخرج﴾; and the clause ﴿يعلم ما يلج ...﴾ is a third khabar (predicate) of ﴿هو﴾, or a ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (ما ينزل): conjoined to ﴿ما يلج﴾; (من السماء): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينزل﴾; (ما يعرج): conjoined to ﴿ما يلج﴾; (فيها): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعرج﴾.
﴿وهو الرحيم الغفور﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (هو): mubtadaʾ (subject); (الرحيم): first khabar (predicate); (الغفور): second khabar.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وقال الذين كفروا لا تأتينا الساعة﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (قال): past verb; (الذين): fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. (لا): negating; (تأتينا): imperfect verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الساعة): fāʿil; and the clause ﴿وقال الذين كفروا...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿قل بلى وربي لتأتينكم﴾: (قل): imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (بلى): a particle of reply, cancelling the negation in their saying ﴿لا تأتينا الساعة﴾; the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; (ربي): a noun in the genitive by the wāw of the oath, and the yāʾ of the speaker is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لتأتينكم): the lām occurs in the response to the oath; (تأتينكم): imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "it" (هي).
﴿عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض﴾: (عالم): an adjective of ﴿ربي﴾, or a badal (substitute); (الغيب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿لا يعزب﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿ربي﴾; (عنه): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يعزب﴾; (مثقال): fāʿil (agent); (ذرة): muḍāf ilayhi; (في السماوات): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of ﴿مثقال ذرة﴾ or a ḥāl from it; (ولا في الأرض): conjoined to ﴿في السماوات﴾.
﴿ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (لا): negating; (أصغر): mubtadaʾ (subject); (من ذلك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أصغر﴾; (ولا أكبر): conjoined to ﴿أصغر﴾; (إلا): particle of restriction; (في كتاب): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of (أصغر); (مبين): an adjective. Alternatively, ﴿ولا أصغر﴾ and ﴿ولا أكبر﴾ are conjoined to (مثقال), and on this view ﴿إلا في كتاب﴾ is an emphasis of the negation in ﴿لا يعزب﴾, as though He said: "but rather it is in a clear Book."

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات﴾: the lām is for causation; (يجزي): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) (أن) after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb is genitive by the lām, and the lām of causation and its genitive are attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأتينكم) or to His saying ﴿لا يعزب﴾; (الذين): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. (عملوا): past verb, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil; (الصالحات): mafʿūl bihi; and the clause ﴿عملوا الصالحات﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾.
﴿أولئك لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم﴾: (أولئك): mubtadaʾ (subject); (لهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of ﴿مغفرة﴾; (مغفرة): postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause ﴿لهم مغفرة﴾ is the khabar of (أولئك); (رزق): conjoined to (مغفرة); (كريم): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك لهم عذاب من رجز أليم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (الذين): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿سعوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. (في آياتنا): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سعوا﴾, on the assumption of an implied muḍāf, i.e. "in invalidating Our signs by attacking them or describing them as sorcery and poetry." (معاجزين): ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in ﴿سعوا﴾; (أولئك): mubtadaʾ; (لهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (عذاب): postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause ﴿لهم عذاب﴾ is the khabar of (أولئك), and the clause ﴿أولئك لهم عذاب﴾ is the khabar of ﴿الذين﴾; (من رجز): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of (عذاب); (أليم): a second adjective of (عذاب); and the clause ﴿والذين سعوا...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ويرى الذين أوتوا العلم الذي أنزل إليك من ربك هو الحق﴾: the wāw is resumptive and (يرى) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); or the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿يرى﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by conjunction with (يجزي), if ﴿ليجزي﴾ is attached to ﴿لتأتينكم﴾. (الذين): fāʿil (agent) of (يرى); (أوتوا): passive past verb, and the wāw of the group is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (العلم): second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أوتوا﴾; the clause ﴿أوتوا العلم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. (الذي): first object of (يرى), and the clause ﴿أُنزل﴾ is the ṣila of (الذي), a clause with no grammatical position. (إليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); (من ربك): a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to (أنزل); (هو): a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; (الحق): second object of (يرى); and the clause ﴿ويرى الذين أوتوا...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿ويهدي إلى صراط العزيز الحميد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (يهدي): conjoined to ﴿الحق﴾, the verb being conjoined to the noun because it has the sense of one. Or the wāw is circumstantial and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الذي أنزل﴾, with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and it guides" (وهو يهدي). Or the wāw is resumptive. The fāʿil (agent) of (يهدي) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to ﴿الذي أنزل﴾; (إلى صراط): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يهدي); (العزيز): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الحميد): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وقال الذين كفروا هل ندلكم على رجل ينبئكم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (قال): past verb; (الذين): fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. (هل): interrogative particle; (ندلكم): imperfect verb, latent (mustatir) agent and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (على رجل): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ندلكم﴾; and the clause ﴿ينبئكم﴾ is an adjective of (رجل).
﴿إذا مزقتم كل ممزق﴾: (إذا): an adverb of future time attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, the implied form being "you will be resurrected and requited at the time of your being torn apart." (مزقتم): passive past verb, the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the mīm is the sign of the plural. (كل): standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb). (ممزق): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause ﴿إذا مزقتم كل ممزق﴾ is parenthetical, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿إنكم لفي خلق جديد﴾: (إنكم): (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters) and ﴿كم﴾ is its noun; the lām is the emphasising shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿في خلق﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of (إن); (جديد): an adjective; and the clause ﴿إنكم لفي خلق جديد﴾ stands in place of the second and third objects of the verb (ينبئكم).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿أفترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة﴾: the hamza is interrogative; (افترى): past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); (على الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (افترى); ﴿كذبا﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb (افترى), i.e. "he fabricated and invented a lie," or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "he fabricated for the sake of lying," or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he fabricated while being a liar," and it is an emphasising ḥāl. (أم): a conjunction counterbalancing the interrogative hamza; (به): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (جنة): postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
