Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied form is "the possessor of the truth has come", i.e. the Book containing the true proofs and arguments. (وَما يُبْدِئُ الْباطِلُ): Saʿīd reported from Qatāda; he said: falsehood is Iblīs; and the implied form in Arabic is "the possessor of falsehood". Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: falsehood is the [false] gods; and he said: «وما يبدئ وما يعيد», i.e. it does not give life and does not cause death. Qatāda said: (ما يُبْدِئُ) «وما يعيد» — it does not create and does not resurrect. Others said: «ما يُبْدِئُ الْباطِلُ», i.e. it does not initiate an argument, and «ما يُعِيدُ», it does not relate an argument from someone else. The first «ما» is in the position of the accusative by «يبدئ», and the second «ما» in the position of the accusative by «يعيد». Abū Isḥāq said: it is better that «ما» be negative.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: (قُلْ إِنْ ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّما أَضِلُّ عَلى نَفْسِي): a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and likewise (وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِما يُوحِي إِلَيَّ رَبِّي). If you make «ما» mean «الذي» (that which), the hāʾ [referring pronoun] is omitted; and if you make it a maṣdar (verbal noun), it does not need a referring pronoun. (إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ), i.e. He hears whoever calls on Him, and is near in answering him.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: (وَلَوْ تَرى إِذْ فَزِعُوا فَلا فَوْتَ): the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "Were you to see when they are terrified, you would see something from which a strong lesson is taken"; i.e. «فلا فوت لهم» — there is no escape for them, i.e. escape is not possible for them.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read (وَأَنَّى لَهُمُ التَّناوُشُ) with hamza [«التناؤش»]. Abū ʿUbayd considered this reading far-fetched, because «التناؤش» is remoteness, so it would be: "How could they have remoteness from a far place?" Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading is permissible and good, and it has two explanations in the speech of the Arabs, and one need not take it in this far-fetched way. One of the two explanations is that the original is without hamza, and then the wāw was given hamza because the vowel on it is weak; that is frequent in the speech of the Arabs. In the muṣḥaf transmitted by the many from the many is (وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ) [al-Mursalāt: 11], the original being «وُقِّتَتْ», because it is derived from «الوقت» (time). And one says, as the plural of «دار»: «أدؤر». The other explanation has been mentioned by Abū Isḥāq; he said: it is derived from «النئيش», which is movement with slowness, i.e. whence will they have movement towards what has become remote, when they disbelieved in it before?

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: (وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ): the Arabs say of everyone who speaks of what he has no right to [know]: "He hurls and casts at the unseen." (مِنْ مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ) is a comparison to one who throws and does not hit with his throw. Whoever read «وَيُقْذَفُونَ» [passive], its meaning according to him is: it is hurled at them by those who lead them astray and misguide them. [Translator's note: the source prints this second reading with the same vowelling as the first, (وَيَقْذِفُونَ); the variant meant is evidently the passive «ويُقذَفون».]

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: (وَحِيلَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ ما يَشْتَهُونَ): it was said: a barrier was placed between them and escape from the punishment; and it was said: a barrier was placed between them and what they desired in this world of their wealth and families. The position of Qatāda is that the meaning is that they desired that it be accepted from them that they obey Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and stop at what He commands them, and a barrier was placed between them and that, because that was only [possible] in this world, and it had passed away at that time. The original of «حِيل» is «حُوِل»; the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the ḥāʾ, so it changed into a yāʾ, and its vowel was dropped because of its heaviness. [Translator's note: the source says «فقلبت حركة الواو على الحاء», literally "the vowel of the wāw was turned onto the ḥāʾ".] (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا فِي شَكٍّ), i.e. in the world, and about Divine Unity; (مُرِيبٍ), i.e. causing suspicion.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: [Translator's note: the entry concerns ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾.] ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) or badal (substitute); it may be in the position of the nominative by an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ (subject), and in the position of the accusative in the sense of "I mean" (aʿnī). Sībawayh related: الحمد لله أهل الحمد ("Praise be to Allah, the One worthy of praise") with the accusative, the nominative and the genitive. ﴿وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَأْتِينَا السَّاعَةُ قُلْ بَلى وَرَبِّي﴾: an oath, and the answer is ﴿لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ﴾. The people of Medina read عالمُ الغيب with the nominative, because the answer to the oath has already come first, so the nominative is good, as mubtadaʾ (subject) with what follows as its khabar (predicate); it may also be nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, and the accusative is permissible in the sense of "I mean". Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read ﴿عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ﴾ as a naʿt (adjective); and the rest of the Kufans read علّامِ الغيب, also in the genitive as a naʿt. عالم is for a little and a lot, and علّام is for a lot only; the usual and most fitting in the like of this is عالم الغيب, whereas if you say علّام الغيوب, علّام is more fitting. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Kisāʾī read لا يعزِب with kasra on the zāy; one says عزب يعزُب and يعزِب. Al-Farrāʾ said: the kasra is dearer to me, and it is the reading of al-Aʿmash. ﴿وَلا أَصْغَرُ مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْبَرُ﴾: with fatḥa [i.e. أصغرَ, أكبرَ], conjoining them to «ذرّة»; and the reading of the generality is with the nominative, by conjunction to مثقال. [Translator's note: the Quranic quotation in the printed text bears the nominative vowelling, while the remark refers to the reading with fatḥa.]

nahhas-irab:4-5.t:
﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾: accusative [subjunctive] by the lām of purpose (lām kay); the implied meaning is "it will surely come to you, so that He may recompense".
Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read ﴿أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ﴾ with the nominative [أليمٌ], as a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وَيَرَى﴾ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to ليجزي; it may be in the position of the nominative as resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ is in the position of the nominative by يرى. ﴿أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾: [العلم is] the khabar of [the verb] whose agent is not named (i.e. the passive) [Translator's note: so in the text; the object of the passive verb is evidently meant]. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the first object of يرى. ﴿هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾: [الحقّ is] the second object, and «هو» is a separating pronoun (fāṣila), which the Kufans call ʿimād ("support"). The nominative is also permissible, with «هو» as mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الحقّ» its khabar (predicate). According to all the grammarians the accusative is more frequent where there is the alif and lām, and likewise with an indefinite noun that does not take the alif and lām and so resembles a definite one. If the khabar is a known proper name, as in your saying كان أخوك هو زيد ("your brother was Zayd"), al-Farrāʾ claimed that the preferred choice in it is the nominative, and likewise كان أبو محمد هو عمرو.
His reason for preferring the nominative is that, since it has no alif and lām, it resembles the indefinite in the saying كان زيد هو جالس ("Zayd was, he is sitting"), because in this only the nominative is permissible.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى رَجُلٍ﴾: if you wish you may assimilate the lām into the nūn, because of its closeness to it. ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾: the meaning is "he says to you". «إذا» is in the position of the accusative, and what governs it is مزّقتم. What governs it cannot be ينبئكم, because he is not informing them at that time; nor can what governs it be what follows إنّ, because that does not govern what precedes it. Abū Isḥāq permitted what governs it to be omitted, the implied meaning being: "when you have been utterly torn apart, you will be resurrected".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿أَفْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ بَلِ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ فِي الْعَذابِ وَالضَّلالِ الْبَعِيدِ﴾ (8) ﴿أَفْتَرى﴾: when the interrogative alif entered, the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was dispensed with, so you dropped it; and the interrogative alif has fatḥa to distinguish it from the connecting alif.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ مِنَّا فَضْلًا﴾: two objects. ﴿يا جِبالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ وَالطَّيْرَ﴾: i.e. echo back the plaintive chanting; the mountains would answer him when he recited the Psalms. It is from آب يؤوب, when one returns. والطيرُ with the nominative is the reading of al-Aʿraj and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. The nominative is from two angles: one is by conjunction to جبال, and the other by conjunction to the implied pronoun in أوّبي; that is good because after it comes «معه». The accusative, according to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, is in the sense of "and We subjected the birds to him". Al-Kisāʾī said: it is conjoined to فضلا, i.e. "We gave him the birds". According to Sībawayh it is conjoined to the position, i.e. "We called the mountains and the birds". It may be a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), as you say استوى الماءُ والخشبةَ ("the water rose level with the post"), i.e. with the post. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq permit قمت وزيداً ("I stood up with Zayd"). ﴿وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِيدَ﴾: it is said:
he was the first for whom iron was made subservient; and it is said that he was given such strength that he could bend iron — and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best about that. Al-Ḥasan said: David ﷺ would take the iron and it would be in his hand like dough, and he would make coats of mail from it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿أَنِ اعْمَلْ سابِغاتٍ﴾: Abū Isḥāq has two answers on it: one is that «أن» is in the sense of أي, explicative (mufassira), conveying the meaning "We said to him: Make"; the other answer is that it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "and We softened iron for him for it [i.e. for making them]", and أن is joined to the imperative form. ﴿سابِغاتٍ﴾ is in the position of the accusative; the adjective stands in place of the thing described, i.e. "make ample coats of mail". دروع is feminine when it is [coats of mail] for war, while درع المرأة (a woman's chemise) is masculine. ﴿وَقَدِّرْ فِي السَّرْدِ﴾: Ibn ʿUyayna said from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid: [it is] the measure of the nail: it should not be thin so that it works loose, nor thick so that it splits it [the ring].

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ﴾: al-Kisāʾī made it co-ordinated with ﴿وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِيدَ﴾ and said the meaning is:
"And We made the wind soft (gentle) for Solomon." Abū Isḥāq said: the implied meaning is "and We subjected the wind to Solomon". ʿĀṣim read ولسليمانَ الريحُ with the nominative [Translator's note: the printed quotation bears the accusative vowelling; the nominative is meant], as mubtadaʾ (subject), or by [the verb of] being settled (al-istiqrār), i.e. "to Solomon belongs the wind, established", and that same meaning is in it. If someone says: when you say أعطيت زيداً ديناراً ولعمرٍو درهمٌ ("I gave Zayd a dinar, and ʿAmr has a dirham"), using the nominative, it does not carry the meaning of the first, and it is possible that you did not give him the dirham — it is answered: the matter is so, [but] the verse is otherwise in meaning; it is known that no one subjected it except Allah, Majestic and Mighty. ﴿غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ﴾: i.e. a month's journey; and likewise ﴿وَرَواحُها شَهْرٌ﴾. Al-Aʿmash related from al-Minhāl from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When Solomon ﷺ sat, four hundred thousand chairs would be set up around him; then the chiefs of mankind would sit next to him, the lowly of mankind next to them, the chiefs of the jinn next to the lowly of mankind, and the lowly of the jinn next to them. Over every chair was appointed a bird that attended to it; then the wind would carry them, and the birds would shade them from the sun. He would set out in the morning from Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) to Iṣṭakhr and take his midday rest there, then set out in the afternoon from Iṣṭakhr and spend the night in Jerusalem. Then Ibn ʿAbbās recited ﴿غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ وَرَواحُها شَهْرٌ﴾. ﴿وَمِنَ الْجِنِّ مَنْ يَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾: «من» is in the position of the accusative in the sense of "and We subjected"; and it may be in the position of the nominative, as preceded regarding الريح. ﴿وَمَنْ يَزِغْ مِنْهُمْ عَنْ أَمْرِنا نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾: a condition and its apodosis. ﴿مَنْ﴾ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and it is complete.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ ما يَشاءُ مِنْ مَحارِيبَ وَتَماثِيلَ﴾: the two are diptotes because this plural has no counterpart among singulars and is not pluralised as other plurals are pluralised. المحراب in the language is any elevated place; that towards which one prays is called a miḥrāb because it ought to be elevated and honoured. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «من محاريب», i.e. of mosques; and تماثيل, he said: images. Some said: making images is permissible because of this verse and because of what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, related about the Messiah ﷺ. Others said: the prohibition of them from the Prophet ﷺ is authentic, as is the threat against whoever makes them or takes them up; so he ﷺ abrogated what had been permitted before him. There was wisdom in that, because he ﷺ was sent when images were being worshipped, and it was most beneficial to remove them. ﴿وَجِفانٍ كَالْجَوابِ وَقُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ﴾: it is preferable that it be with yāʾ [i.e. كالجوابي]; whoever drops the yāʾ says: the way of the alif and lām is to enter an indefinite noun without changing it from its state; so since one says «جوابٍ», when the alif and lām entered it was left in its state with the yāʾ dropped. The singular of الجوابي is جابية, which is the great cauldron and the large basin into which a thing is collected (yujbā), i.e. gathered; from this is جبيت الخراج ("I collected the land-tax") and جبيت الجراد, i.e. I spread out a cloak and gathered them into it. However, Layth related from Mujāhid that he said:
الجوابي is the plural of جوبة. Abū Jaʿfar said: الجوبة is a large hollow in a mountain in which rainwater collects. ﴿وَقُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ﴾: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they are copper cauldrons found in Persia. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they are cauldrons that were made from the rocks of the mountains. ﴿اعْمَلُوا آلَ داوُدَ شُكْراً﴾: i.e. it is said to them.
﴿آلَ داوُدَ﴾: a vocative in a construct (nidāʾ muḍāf). According to Abū Isḥāq the accusative of شكرا is from two angles: one is "work for the sake of thanks", i.e. so that you may thank Allah, Majestic and Mighty; and the other is that the implied meaning is "give thanks with thanks" [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)]. ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبادِيَ الشَّكُورُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). الشكور is for intensification only, while شاكر applies to little and much. Thanks (al-shukr) is only for a specific thing, and praise (al-ḥamd) is more general than it.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
﴿مِنْسَأَتَهُ﴾ is the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr, and the Kufans read it with hamza. [Translator's note: so in the printed text; from what follows the reading of the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr is مِنْسَاتَه without hamza.] Its derivation indicates that it has a hamza, because it is derived from نسأته, i.e. I delayed it and pushed it; so it was called منسأة because a thing is pushed and delayed with it. Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said: it is the staff. Whoever read (منساته) replaced the hamza with alif. If someone says: substitution for the hamza is ugly and is permissible only in poetry, remotely and anomalously, and the like of this would not escape Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, especially as the people of Medina follow this reading — the answer to this is that the Arabs used substitution in this word and pronounced it thus, as substitution occurs elsewhere, and it is not made a basis for analogy; so much so that Abū ʿAmr said: "I do not know what it is from,
except that it has no hamza." And this is the speech of the learned, because what has a hamza may have its hamza left out, whereas what has no hamza may not be given a hamza in any way. ﴿فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ الْجِنُّ﴾: his death. [Translator's note: something appears to be missing before the next sentence, as no first speaker is named.] Someone else said: the meaning is "the matter of the jinn became clear", like ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82]. And it is said that the meaning is "the jinn became clear to mankind". In the exegesis with sound chains of transmission there is an explanation of the meaning: Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Solomon son of David, Allah's blessings be upon them both, remained for a year without his death being known, leaning on his staff, while the jinn went about what he had commanded them; then he fell after a year. Ibn ʿAbbās read: فلما خرّ تبيّنت الإنس أن لو كان الجنّ يعلمون الغيب ما لبثوا في العذاب المهين ("When he fell, mankind realised that, had the jinn known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment"). Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading from Ibn ʿAbbās is by way of exegesis. As for ﴿أَنْ﴾, its position is the nominative as a badal (substitute) for الجنّ, i.e. "it became clear that, had the jinn known the unseen…"; this is a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). It may also be in the position of the accusative in the sense of the lām [i.e. "because"].

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
﴿لَقَدْ كانَ لِسَبَإٍ﴾: fully declined, with tanwīn, as the name of the tribe-group (ḥayy); originally it is the name of a man, as came by specification (tawqīf) from the Prophet ﷺ. Abū ʿAmr read لقد كان لسبأَ without full declension [Translator's note: the printed quotation shows the tanwīn form; the diptote is meant], making it the name of the tribe (qabīla); this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, who argued that it is the name of a tribe from the fact that after it comes ﴿فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ﴾; if it were as it was [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps "as he said" is meant], it would have been في مساكنها. ﴿آيَةٌ﴾ is the noun (ism) of kāna, i.e. a sign indicating the power of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and His favour upon His servants: that He made for the people of Sabaʾ two gardens, on the right and the left, and of what collected of rain between two mountains, at whose face was a dyke (musannāt). Yaḥyā ibn Sulaymān al-Juʿfī said: al-musannāt is what the people of Egypt call al-jisr ("the dam"); they would open it when they wished, and when their garden had been watered they would close it. ﴿جَنَّتانِ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for الآية; it may be nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); آية may be made accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna; and جنتين may also be made accusative as the khabar, outside the Quran.
The implied meaning [of what follows] is: it was said to them: "Eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him." Al-Farrāʾ said: the statement is complete [here]. ﴿بَلْدَةٌ﴾: nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is a land"; ﴿وَرَبٌّ﴾ likewise by an implied mubtadaʾ; ﴿غَفُورٌ﴾ is its naʿt (adjective). As for في مساكنهم, it is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Abū ʿAmr. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Ḥamza read ﴿فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. مَسْكَنِهم with fatḥa on the kāf], and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read في مسكِنهم with kasra on the kāf. Abū Jaʿfar said: «مساكن» is clearer in this, because it unites the wording and the meaning. If you say مسكنهم, there are two analyses in it: one is that it is a singular conveying a plural, and the other is that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), which is neither dualised nor pluralised, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلى أَبْصارِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 7], where السمع came in the singular; and likewise ﴿فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 55]. Whoever says مسكِن with kasra on the kāf makes it like مسجد, and it is outside analogy; its like is found only by hearing (samāʿ).

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فَأَعْرَضُوا فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ الْعَرِمِ﴾: ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl said: «العرم» is the dyke (al-musannāt). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: العرم is any barrier between two things, which is what is called al-sikr ("the weir"); it is the plural of عرمة. ﴿وَبَدَّلْناهُمْ بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ﴾: Abū ʿAmr read ذواتَي أُكُلِ خمطٍ without tanwīn, in a construct. [Translator's note: the printed quotation of Abū ʿAmr's reading shows the tanwīn; the construct form is meant.] The exegetes and al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: «الخمط» is the arāk tree. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: الخمط is anything that has changed to what is not desirable; milk is khamṭ when it turns sour. The better reading in his view is ﴿ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ﴾ with tanwīn, as a naʿt (adjective) of أكل or a badal (substitute) for it, because in his view the produce is the khamṭ itself. As for the construct, the way to its permissibility is that its implied meaning be "possessing produce of sourness" or "produce of bitterness". ﴿وَشَيْءٍ مِنْ سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: it is the samur (acacia).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ بِما كَفَرُوا﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: «ذلك» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "We recompensed them with that". وهل يُجازى إلا الكفورُ ("And is any recompensed except the ungrateful?") is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; and the Kufans except ʿĀṣim read ﴿وَهَلْ نُجازِي إِلَّا الْكَفُورَ﴾ ("And do We recompense any except the ungrateful?"). This is preferable according to Abū ʿUbayd, because before it is «جزيناهم», and He did not say جوزوا ("they were recompensed"). [Translator's note: the attribution of the two readings appears reversed in the printed text; in the standard transmission it is Ḥafṣ ʿan ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī who read نُجازي.] Abū Jaʿfar said: there is latitude in this matter, and the meaning in it is clear: if one person said "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, created Adam from clay" and another said "Adam was created from clay", the meaning would be the same. In the verse there is a question; I know of none in the sūra harder than it. It is asked: what is the meaning of "And is any recompensed except the ungrateful?", when He did not mention the people of sins other than the disbelievers? The scholars have discussed this. Some said:
no one is recompensed with the like of this recompense, which is extirpation and destruction, except whoever disbelieves. As for Quṭrub, his answer on this verse is otherwise, because he applied it to the people of sins other than the disbelievers, following his school, and his saying [was]: "whoever is ungrateful for the blessings and commits major sins". The best of what has been said about this verse, and the most eminent of what has been related about it, is that al-Ḥasan said: "like for like". Ayyūb related from Abū Mulayka [Translator's note: so in the text; Ibn Abī Mulayka is the known narrator] from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever is brought to account is ruined." I said: "O Prophet of Allah, then what of His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿فَسَوْفَ يُحاسَبُ حِساباً يَسِيراً﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 8]?" He said: "That is only the presentation; and whoever is scrutinised in the reckoning is ruined." Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a sound chain. Its explanation is that the disbeliever is requited for his deeds and brought to account for them, and whatever good he did is nullified. What makes this clear to you is His saying, Majestic and Mighty, in the first ﴿ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ بِما كَفَرُوا﴾ and in the second «وهل يجازى»: the meaning of «يجازى» is "he is requited for what he did", and the meaning of «جزيناهم» is "We paid them in full". This is the literal sense of the language, even though جازى occurs in the sense of جزى figuratively.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْقُرَى الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها قُرىً ظاهِرَةً﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās said: الظاهرة is the elevated. ﴿وَقَدَّرْنا فِيهَا السَّيْرَ﴾: i.e. We made it by measure, so that they travel and spend the night in a village. Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿وَقَدَّرْنا فِيهَا السَّيْرَ﴾, i.e. We made [the distance] between every two villages half a day; this is the measuring.
﴿سِيرُوا فِيها لَيالِيَ وَأَيَّاماً﴾: two adverbs (ẓarf). ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾: as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
﴿فَقالُوا رَبَّنا باعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفارِنا﴾: there are six variant readings in it. [Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes the readings has largely been lost in the printed text; the intended forms, reconstructed from the author's explanations, are given in square brackets.] Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Mālik, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿رَبَّنا باعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفارِنا﴾. Mujāhid, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read ربّنا بعد بين أسفارنا [رَبَّنا بَعِّدْ]. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya read, and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ṣāliḥ, ربّنا باعد بين أسفارنا [رَبُّنا باعَدَ]. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read, and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, ربّنا بعّد بين أسفارنا [رَبُّنا بَعَّدَ]. Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, the brother of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, read فقالوا ربّنا بعد بين أسفارنا [رَبَّنا بَعُدَ بَيْنُ]. These are five readings. Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Isḥāq related the sixth: ربّنا بعد بين أسفارنا [رَبَّنا بَعُدَ بَيْنَ]. Abū Jaʿfar said: in the first reading ربّنا is accusative as a vocative in a construct (nidāʾ muḍāf); it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because its meaning is "I called, I invoked". Likewise the second reading. «باعِد» and «بعِّد» are one in meaning, as you say قارِب and قرِّب. The meaning, according to what Muḥammad ibn Thawr related from Maʿmar from Qatāda, who said: they were secure; they would go out on their journeys without taking provisions, spending the night in one village and taking the midday rest in another; then they became insolent towards the blessing and said: "Our Lord, lengthen [the distance] between our journeys", so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, punished them.
In the third reading «ربُّنا» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «باعَدَ» is a past verb in the position of the khabar (predicate); likewise the fourth. Ibn ʿAbbās explained it; he said: they complained that their Lord had lengthened [the distance] between their journeys. The fifth reading is ربّنا بعُد بينُ أسفارنا: «ربّنا» is a vocative in a construct, then they made a statement after that, saying «بعُد بينُ أسفارنا» ("the span of our journeys has grown long"), with «بين» nominative by the verb, i.e. what connects to our journeys has grown long. The sixth reading is like this, except that it makes «بين» accusative as an adverb (ẓarf); its implied form in Arabic is "our travelling has grown long between our journeys". When these readings differ in their meanings, it may not be said that one of them is better than another — that is not said of reports when their meanings differ — rather, He reported of them that they prayed that [the distance] between their journeys be lengthened, out of insolence and arrogance, and He reported that when that was done to them they told of it and complained, as Ibn ʿAbbās said. ﴿وَظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾: i.e. by their disbelief. ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُمْ أَحادِيثَ﴾: i.e. their stories are told; its implied form in Arabic is "possessors of tales". ﴿وَمَزَّقْناهُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾: i.e. when what befell them befell them, they dispersed and were torn apart. Al-Shaʿbī said:
So the Anṣār joined Yathrib, Ghassān Syria, Asad ʿUmān [Translator's note: so in the text; Azd is the usual name in this account], and Khuzāʿa Tihāma. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾: «صبّار» is the intensive of صابر. The ṣābir is the one who restrains himself from sins; he is praised with this name. If you mean that he persisted in sin, only صابر عن كذا ... is used for it. [Translator's note: this sentence is garbled in the printed text and is translated as written.] He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّما يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾ [al-Zumar: 10].

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾: there are four variant readings in it. [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variants has largely been lost in the printed text; the intended forms, reconstructed from the author's explanations, are given in square brackets.] Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read — and it is related from Mujāhid — ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَ﴾ with the light form, ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ﴾ with the nominative, ﴿ظَنَّهُ﴾ with the accusative. Ibn ʿAbbās, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿صَدَّقَ﴾ with the doubled form. Abū al-Hajhāj read ولقد صدق عليهم إبليسَ ظنُّه, with إبليس accusative and ظنّه nominative. Abū Ḥātim said: in my view this reading has no justification, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best. Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Farrāʾ permitted this reading, and Abū Isḥāq mentioned it and said:
the meaning is: Iblīs's opinion proved Iblīs right, by their following him. The fourth reading is ولقد صدق عليهم إبليسُ ظنُّه, with both إبليس and ظنّه nominative. The first reading, ولقد صدَق عليهم إبليسُ ظنَّه, means "in his opinion"; Abū Isḥāq said: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). The second reading, ولقد صدّق عليهم إبليسُ ظنَّه, has «ظنّه» accusative by the verb falling on it [as its object]. Mujāhid said: he held an opinion, and it turned out as he thought, so he confirmed his opinion. From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Iblīs [said]: "Adam was created from clay, so he is weak, and I am from fire; I will surely bring his offspring under my sway, except a few"; and it was as he said. Al-Ḥasan said: he did not strike them with a whip or a stick; he only held an opinion, and it turned out as he thought, through his whispering. ﴿إِلَّا فَرِيقاً مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: accusative by the exception. There are two views on it: one is that some of the believers are meant by it; as for Ibn ʿAbbās, it is reported from him that he said: they are all the believers.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: [Translator's note: the entry concerns ﴿وَما كانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ﴾.] ﴿مِنْ﴾ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. The exegetes say: السلطان is the proof (al-ḥujja). ﴿إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, already knew that as the unseen; this is the knowledge of what is witnessed, by which the proof becomes binding. This is the view of most of the philologists. According to some of them it is figurative, i.e. so that this be His knowledge on which He requites. A third view, which is the school of al-Farrāʾ, is that the meaning is "except that We may know that in your estimation", as He said ﴿أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 27], i.e. according to your claim and in your estimation.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾: there is an ellipsis in the passage; the meaning is: Say: call upon those whom you claimed to be gods for you besides Allah, that they may benefit you or ward off from you what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has decreed against you; for they do not possess that. ﴿لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّماواتِ وَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما لَهُمْ فِيهِما مِنْ شِرْكٍ وَما لَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ ظَهِيرٍ﴾: al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī said: i.e. of any helper.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
﴿أَذِنَ﴾ and أُذِنَ [Translator's note: the vowelling of the two forms is not shown in the printed text] are one in meaning, as has passed regarding وهل يُجازى [Sabaʾ: 17]. «مَن» here is for the intercessors, and it may be for those interceded for. Abū Isḥāq claimed that [its being] for the intercessors fits the meaning better; he said: because after it is ﴿حَتَّى إِذا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, so this would be for the angels, Allah's blessings be upon them. There are five readings in this. [Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes the readings has largely been lost in the printed text; the intended forms, reconstructed from the descriptions, are given in square brackets.] The reading of the generality is ﴿حَتَّى إِذا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾; and from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid: حتى إذا فَزَّع عن قلوبهم, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the zāy. These two readings have one meaning, i.e. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, removed fear from their hearts, i.e. the fear passed beyond them. Sībawayh says likewise regarding the Arabs' saying رميت عن القوس, i.e. my shooting passed beyond the bow; and we have mentioned its meaning. Haytham [Translator's note: probably Hushaym is meant] related from ʿAwf from al-Ḥasan that he read حتى إذا فُرِّغ عن قلوبهم, with ḍamma on the fāʾ and with an undotted rāʾ followed by a dotted ghayn; and Abū Mijlaz read likewise. Maṭar al-Warrāq related from al-Ḥasan حتى إذا فزّع عن قلوبهم [فَرَّغ]. The meaning of these two readings comes back to the meaning of the first two, because the meaning is: until, when the fear was emptied from their hearts, [it was] removed from their hearts. However, Mujāhid said in explaining this verse, according to what Warqāʾ related from him via [Ibn] Abī Najīḥ:
it is on the Day of Resurrection. He said: when the covering is removed. Ayyūb and Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl related from al-Ḥasan حتى إذا فُرِغ عن قلوبهم, with ḍamma on the fāʾ, with a light (undoubled) undotted rāʾ followed by a dotted ghayn. These transmissions from al-Ḥasan have sound chains, with no flaw in any of those who related them, and all of them are authentic from him. ﴿قالُوا ماذا قالَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾: «ماذا» is in the position of the accusative by قال; and «ما» may be in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with «ذا» in the position of the khabar (predicate), its meaning being that of الذي ("that which"). ﴿قالُوا الْحَقَّ﴾: on the basis that «ماذا» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "He said the truth"; and the nominative of «الحقّ» is permissible on the basis that ما is in the position of the nominative. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar. «العليّ» is the Compeller, the Exalted; and «الكبير» is the Lord to whom one turns.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلَهُ ٱلْحَمْدُ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
It is [the same as] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أنِ الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: Wise in His command, All-Aware of His creation.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا﴾.
That is, what enters it of rain and other things, and what comes out of it of vegetation and other things.
﴿وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا﴾:
from عَرَج يعرُج, when one ascends.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لاَ تَأْتِينَا ٱلسَّاعَةُ قُلْ بَلَىٰ وَرَبِّي لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ عَالِمِ ٱلْغَيْبِ﴾.
That is: Yes indeed, by my Lord, the Knower of the unseen, it will surely come to you.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لاَ يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَلاَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Abū Yaḥyā narrated from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿لاَ يَعْزُبُ﴾: is not absent.
"Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb" read: ﴿لاَ يَعْزِبُ﴾, and it is a well-known dialect form; one says عَزَبَ يَعْزُبُ and يَعْزِبُ when something is far away and absent.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ سَعَوْا فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا مُعَاجِزِينَ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِّن رِّجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: They thought that they could escape Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and they will never escape Him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says عَاجَزَه and أعجَزَه when one contends with someone and outstrips him. Whoever reads ﴿مُعَجِّزِينَ﴾ means: holding the believers back (discouraging them); this is what Ibn al-Zubayr said.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
Qatāda said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾:
That is, when the earth has eaten you, and you have become bones and crumbled remains.
﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ [that is, you will be brought to life and resurrected]?

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
Then He informed them that the One who created the heavens and the earth is able to do that, and to hasten the punishment for them, and said:
﴿أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَىٰ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلأَرْضِ إِن نَّشَأْ نَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ ٱلأَرْضَ أَوْ نُسْقِطْ عَلَيْهِمْ كِسَفاً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾? [Verse 9].
That is, a piece.
﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَةً لِّكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُّنِيبٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, repentant.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ مِنَّا فَضْلاً يٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ﴾.
﴿يٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ﴾: that is, We said.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū Maysara said: ﴿أَوِّبِي﴾, that is, glorify.
Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿أُوبِي مَعَهُ﴾.
What is well known in the language is that one says آبَ يَئُوبُ when one returns and comes back; so the meaning of ﴿أُوْبي﴾ would be: come back [repeatedly] with him in glorification.
And ﴿أَوِّبِي﴾ in the speech of the Arabs has two meanings.
One of them: it is the intensive of "أُوْبي", so on this view the meaning of ﴿أَوِّبي﴾ is: echo [his words] with him in glorification.
(The second): one says أَوَّبَ when one travels by day; so on this view the meaning of ﴿أَوِّبي﴾ is: travel along with him.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلْحَدِيدَ﴾.
Qatāda said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, softened iron for him, and he would work it without fire.
Al-Aʿmash said: Iron was softened for him until it became like threads.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَنِ ٱعْمَلْ سَابِغَاتٍ وَقَدِّرْ فِي ٱلسَّرْدِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, ample coats of mail.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says سَبَغَ the garment, the coat of mail and the like, when it covers all that it is upon and some of it is left over.
Then He said: ﴿وَقَدِّرْ فِي ٱلسَّرْدِ﴾.
Qatāda said: السَّرْدُ is the nail (rivet) in the rings of the coat of mail.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿السَّرْدُ﴾ is the rings.
And السَّردُ in the language is anything made in an orderly and continuous way, its parts close to one another; and from it is سَرْدُ الكلام (continuous speech).
Sībawayh said: And from it is رجل سَرْنَدِيٌّ, that is, bold; he said: because he goes straight forward.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And from it «[Translator's note: the text has ومن قيل, evidently for ومنه قيل]» the one who makes coats of mail is called زَرَّادٌ and سَرَّادٌ.
So the meaning — and it is the view of Mujāhid — is: and measure the rivets in the rings of the coat of mail so that they are of the right proportion: the rivet should not be thick and the ring narrow, so that the ring breaks; nor should you widen the ring and make the rivet small and thin, so that the ring comes loose.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَسَلْنَا لَهُ عَيْنَ ٱلْقِطْرِ﴾.
Qatāda said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made a spring of copper flow.
That is, until it flowed and appeared, and he used it for whatever he wished.
Al-Aʿmash said: It was made to flow for him as water is made to flow.
And it is said: copper had not melted for anyone before him.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَارِيبَ وَتَمَاثِيلَ﴾.
Abū Hilāl narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿مَّحَارِيبَ﴾: places of prayer (masājid); and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said the same.
Mujāhid said: The maḥārīb are [buildings] less than palaces.
And al-maḥārīb in the language are every elevated or noble place.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَتَمَاثِيلَ﴾. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, images.
Mujāhid said: ﴿تماثيل﴾, that is, of copper.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَجِفَانٍ كَٱلْجَوَابِ وَقُدُورٍ رَّاسِيَاتٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿الجوابي﴾ are the watering troughs of camels.
Abū Jaʿfar said: الجابيةُ in the language is the trough in which a thing is collected (yujbā), that is, gathered.
And from it is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
نَفَى الذَمَّ عن آلِ المُحَلَّقِ جَفْنهٌ * كَجَابِيةِ الشَّيْخِ العِرَاقي تَفْهَقُ
(A great bowl, like the brimming trough of the old Iraqi, has driven blame away from the family of al-Muḥallaq.)
And it is also narrated: كجابية السَّيحِ (like the trough of the flowing stream).
Mujāhid said: ﴿رَّاسِيَاتٍ﴾, that is, huge.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿رَّاسِيَاتٍ﴾: they are emptied out [in place] and not carried.
Qatāda said: ﴿رَّاسِيَاتٍ﴾, that is, fixed firmly.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ٱعْمَلُوۤاْ آلَ دَاوُودَ شُكْراً وَقَلِيلٌ مِّنْ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit one day and recited ﴿ٱعْمَلُوۤاْ آلَ دَاوُودَ شُكْراً﴾, and said:
"Three things: whoever is given them has been given the like of what the family of David was given:
- Justice in anger and in contentment.
- Moderation in poverty and in wealth.
- And fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in secret and in public."
Mujāhid said: "When Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said ﴿ٱعْمَلُوۤاْ آلَ دَاوُودَ شُكْراً﴾, David said to Solomon, may Allah bless them both: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has mentioned gratitude; so take over the prayer of the day for me, and I will take over the prayer of the night for you. He said: I am not able to.
He said: Then take over for me — al-Faryābī said: I think he said — until the noon prayer. He said: Yes; and he took it over for him."
Al-Zuhrī said: ﴿ٱعْمَلُوۤاْ آلَ دَاوُودَ شُكْراً﴾, that is, say: Praise be to Allah.
And it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [In] gratitude for what He has bestowed upon you.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا قَضَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَوْتَ مَا دَلَّهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَوْتِهِ إِلاَّ دَابَّةُ الأَرْضِ تَأْكُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: He remained a full year until the termite ate his staff and he fell; then it was known that he had died.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "المِنْسَأة" is the staff.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The staff is called مِنْسأة because with it a thing is driven back and driven along. Ṭarafa said:
أَمُونٍ كأَلْوَاحِ الإرَانِ نَسْأَتُهَا * على لاَحِبٍ كَأَنَّهُ ظَهْرُ بُرْجُدِ
(A trusty she-camel, [her ribs] like the planks of a bier, which I drove on with the staff along a beaten track like the back of a striped cloak.)
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ ٱلْجِنُّ أَن لَّوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْغَيْبَ مَا لَبِثُواْ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ﴾.
Qatāda said: The jinn used to tell mankind that they knew the unseen. When Solomon ﷺ died and the jinn did not know of it, [the matter of] the jinn became clear to mankind: that they do not know the unseen.
This is the best of what has been said about the verse.
The meaning is: the affair of the jinn became clear.
What indicates its soundness is the marfūʿ ḥadīth (traced back to the Prophet).
Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān narrated from ʿAṭāʾ, from al-Sāʾib «[Translator's note: so in the text; the narrator is usually ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib]», from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Solomon, the Prophet of Allah, whenever he prayed, would see a tree growing in front of him, and he would ask it: What is your name? If it was for planting, it was planted; if it was for medicine, it was written down. While he was praying one day, there was a tree growing in front of him, and he said: What is your name? It said: al-Kharnūb (the carob). He said: For what are you? It said: For the ruin of the people of this house. He said: O Allah, conceal my death from the jinn, so that mankind may know that the jinn do not know the unseen. Then he carved it into a staff and leaned on it for a year without their knowing. Then it fell, and mankind knew that the jinn do not know the unseen. They looked into the length of that time and found it to be a year; and the jinn were grateful to the termite."
Qatāda said: And in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿تَبَيَّنَتِ الإِنْسُ أَنْ لَوْ كَانَ الجِنُّ يَعْلَمُونَ الْغَيْبَ مَا لَبِثُوا في العَذَابِ المُهِينِ﴾.
And whoever reads ﴿تُبُيِّنَتِ الجِنُّ﴾ (passive) means: mankind came to see clearly [the truth about] the jinn.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ كَانَ لِسَبَإٍ فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ﴾.
It is narrated that "سَبَأ" is the name of a man; on this view it is a name for the tribe, for those who treat it as a diptote (do not give it tanwīn).
And it is said: it is the name of a place.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ﴾.
That is, a garden on the right and a garden on the left.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾.
The meaning is: this is a good land, and Allah is a Forgiving Lord.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأَعْرَضُواْ فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ ٱلْعَرِمِ﴾.
That is, they turned away from the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and from thanking Him, so We sent upon them the flood of al-ʿarim.
ʿAṭāʾ said: al-ʿarim is the name of the valley.
And it is said: it is the rat that was sent against them.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: (al-ʿarim) is the severe.
And it is said: it is the ʿarim rain, that is, the severe.
Qatāda said: Allah sent a rat against them, and it destroyed their ʿarim — by al-ʿarim he means the dam. He said: So it drowned their gardens and ruined their land as a punishment for them.
This is the best known of what has been said about the meaning of ﴿العَرِم﴾.
A dam is called عَرْمَة, and its plural is عَرِم; it was so named because of its strength; and from it «[Translator's note: the text has ومن قيل, evidently for ومنه قيل]» one says: فلان عَارِم (so-and-so is fierce). The poet said:
* "إذْ يَبْنُونَ مِنْ دُونِ سَيْلِهِ العَرِمَا" * (when they were building the dams against its flood)
* His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَبَدَّلْنَاهُمْ بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَوَاتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ﴾.
Al-ukul is fruit.
Abū Mālik, Mujāhid, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-khamṭ is the arāk tree; and al-Khalīl said the same.
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-khamṭ is every tree that has bitterness and has thorns.
Al-Qutabī said in Adab al-Kātib: a sour [wine] is called khamṭa; and it is said that al-khamṭa is [wine] that has taken on something of the smell [of souring]. And he recited:
عُقَارٌ كمَاءِ النِّيءِ لَيْسَتْ بِخَمْطَةٍ * وَلاَ خَلَّةٍ يَكْوِي الشُّرُوبَ شِهَابُها
(A wine like the juice of raw [meat], neither soured nor turned to vinegar, whose fiery sharpness burns the drinkers.)

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ بِمَا كَفَرُواْ وَهَلْ نُجَٰزِيۤ إِلاَّ ٱلْكَفُورَ﴾.
Ṭāwūs said: It is the close scrutiny in the reckoning; whoever is scrutinized is punished.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What shows you the soundness of this is what Ayyūb narrated from Ibn Abī Mulayka, from ʿĀʾisha, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is called to account is punished." She said: I said: But Allah says: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِي كِتَابَهُ بِيمَينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابَاً يَسِيرَاً﴾. He said: "That is only the presentation; but whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning is punished."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is that the believer has his evil deeds expiated, while the unbeliever's deeds are nullified and he is requited, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْقُرَى ٱلَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا قُرًى ظَاهِرَةً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: Between Yemen and Syria. He said: ﴿ٱلْقُرَى ٱلَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا﴾ is Syria (al-Shām).
Qatāda said: ﴿قُرًى ظَاهِرَةً﴾: connected along the road.
Mujāhid said: Every day they would come upon water.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقَدَّرْنَا فِيهَا ٱلسَّيْرَ سِيرُواْ فِيهَا لَيَالِيَ وَأَيَّاماً آمِنِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: They would set out in the morning and take their midday rest in one village, and set out in the evening and spend the night in another village. They travelled without fear, hunger or thirst. A woman would pass by with her basket on her head and would not return without it being full of fruit, without [her] picking any.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
He said: Then they became insolent with the blessing: ﴿فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا بَاعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا﴾.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَظَلَمُوۤاْ أَنفُسَهُمْ فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya read ﴿رَبُّنَا بَاعَدَ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا﴾ (Our Lord has lengthened the distance between our journeys).
Ibn ʿAbbās said: They complained about their Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur and ʿĪsā read: ﴿رَبَّنَا بَعِّدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan — the brother of al-Ḥusayn «[Translator's note: so in the text; Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan is known as the brother of al-Ḥasan (al-Baṣrī)]» — read: ﴿رَبَّنَا بَعُدَ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا﴾.
The first reading is clearer. The people of tafsīr say: they became insolent with the blessing, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, reported that He punished them for that. However, it is possible that they said this after Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, had lengthened the distance between their journeys; or that, in their insolence, they considered what was near to be far.
The Arabs used to make them proverbial, saying: "تَفَرَّقوا أيْدِيَ سَبأٍ" and "أَيَاديَ سَبَأٍ" (they dispersed like the hands of Saba'), that is, the routes and roads of Saba'.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾.
This is the reading of al-Hajhāj.
And ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾ is permissible [in the sense of]: in his supposition. «[Translator's note: the two quotations are vocalized identically in the text; the second is presumably the reading صَدَقَ without shadda, with ظنَّه accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "proved true in his supposition".]»
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: Iblīs said: I was created from fire, and Adam, may Allah bless him, was created from clay, weak — ﴿لأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيتَهُ إلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
And it is narrated that he said: I misled Adam despite his station and his knowledge, so I am even more capable over his offspring. And so he found his supposition true.
This is made clear by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ وَعَنْ شَمَائِلِهِمْ، وَلاَ تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَاكِرينَ﴾, and His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أجْمَعِينَ. إلاَّ عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ المُخْلَصِينَ﴾. He only said this as a supposition, and his supposition proved true.
Whoever reads ﴿صَدَّقَ﴾ (with shadda) makes الظنّ a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
And whoever puts الظنّ in the nominative and إبليس in the accusative means: the supposition of Iblīs proved true when they followed him.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن سُلْطَانٍ﴾.
That is, any proof (authority).
﴿إِلاَّ لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾, that is, We only tested them with him so that We might know who believes in the Hereafter — with the knowledge of [what is] witnessed; as for the knowledge of the unseen, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows it before it comes to be.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا لَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِّن ظَهِيرٍ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿مِّن ظَهِيرٍ﴾, that is, any helper.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَاعَةُ عِندَهُ إِلاَّ لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: except for the one who is permitted to intercede;
or that it refers to the one interceded for.
The first is clearer, because of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَن قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿حتَّى إذَا فَرَّعَ عن قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, that is, [until] Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, removed the terror from their hearts; one says فزَّعتُه: I removed the terror from him. «[Translator's note: the quoted reading is printed فَرَّعَ (with rāʾ) while the explanation is of فَزَّعَ (with zāy); translated as written.]»
The well-known reading of al-Ḥasan is: ﴿حتى إذا فُرِّغَ عن قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, that is, the terror was emptied out of them.
ʿIkrima said: I heard Abū Hurayra say that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and [a sound] is heard like a chain on smooth rock. They say: What did your Lord say?
And it is said to the one who spoke: The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great.." and he mentioned — and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: "The angels in heaven hear a sound of the revelation like the sound of steel on rock, and they fall down on their foreheads. When [the terror] is removed from them, they say to the messengers: What did your Lord say? And they say: The truth, the truth."
Qatāda said: When the interval (al-fatra) between Jesus and Muḥammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, ended and the revelation came down, the angels fell down prostrating; ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَن قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, that is, [until] it was removed.
﴿قَالُواْ مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾? They said: The truth.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
The meaning is: "Indeed we are upon guidance or in clear error, or you are upon guidance or in clear error".. then [part of it] was omitted.
This is by way of courteous address and of making [them] acknowledge [the truth]; that is: the proofs have become manifest and the truth has become clear — as one says: You know which of us is the liar.
Qatāda said: ﴿ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ بَيْنَنَا﴾, that is, He will judge between us.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلاَّ كَآفَّةً لِّلنَّاسِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, to all people.
And the Prophet ﷺ said: (I have been sent to every red and black one).

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَلاَ بِٱلَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq «[Translator's note: al-Zajjāj]» said: He means the earlier scriptures; and they are the unbelievers of the Arabs.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ مَكْرُ ٱلْلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: That is, rather [it was] your plotting by night and by day.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read ﴿بل مَكَرُّ اللَّيلِ والنَّهارِ﴾, from al-kurūr (the succession, recurring).
Rāshid — he was the one who used to examine the codices in the time of al-Ḥajjāj — read ﴿بَلْ مَكَرَّ اللَّيلِ والنَّهارِ﴾.
The meaning is: [at] the time of the succession of night and day.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ﴾.
That is, its chiefs, its arrogant ones and its leaders.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلاَ أَوْلاَدُكُمْ بِٱلَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِندَنَا زُلْفَىٰ﴾.
The meaning is: your wealth is not that which brings you near, nor are your children those who bring you near; then [one of the two] was omitted.
* His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ جَزَآءُ ٱلضِّعْفِ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ﴾.
That is, the multiplied reward of which We informed you, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا﴾.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُ﴾.
Al-Minhāl narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: without extravagance and without stinginess.
That is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will replace it with reward.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ﴾.
That is, they were not People of the Book, and no prophet was sent to them before Muḥammad ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبلِهِمْ وَمَا بَلَغُواْ مِعْشَارَ مَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, those before these [people] denied, and these have not attained a tenth of what those were given; they were tougher and stronger, and yet they were destroyed.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿مِعْشَارَ﴾ means a tenth. A parallel to this verse is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقدْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِيمَا إنْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُمْ بِوَاحِدَةٍ أَن تَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ مَثْنَىٰ وَفُرَادَىٰ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, one thing I exhort you with: that you stand for Allah; and this was His exhortation to them.
The meaning, according to Qatāda's view: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُمْ﴾ with a single trait; then He made it clear and said: ﴿أَن تَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ مَثْنَىٰ وَفُرَادَىٰ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿بِوَاحِدَةٍ﴾: with obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. And it is said: with [affirming] His oneness.
The meaning on this view is: so that you stand for Allah in twos and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion.
That is, one of you stands alone, and consults another, saying: Do you know of this man ever having lied, or practised sorcery, or soothsaying, or composed poetry? Then reflect after that, for it will be known that what he brought is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And it is said: whoever is perplexed about a matter, then takes counsel about it, then reflects after that, the truth becomes clear to him and he takes heed.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ مَا سَأَلْتُكُم مِّن أَجْرٍ فَهُوَ لَكُمْ﴾.
That is, whatever reward I have asked of you for delivering the message and calling you to accept it, it is yours.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بِٱلْحَقِّ عَلاَّمُ ٱلْغُيُوبِ﴾.
﴿يَقْذِفُ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾, that is, He brings it.
Qatāda said: ﴿بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾, that is, with the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ جَآءَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَمَا يُبْدِىءُ ٱلْبَاطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ﴾.
That is: and what thing does falsehood originate? «[Translator's note: i.e. taking "ما" as interrogative.]»
And it is possible that "ما" is negative.
Qatāda said: ﴿ٱلْبَاطِلُ﴾ is Satan; he neither creates anyone nor resurrects him.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ إِذْ فَزِعُواْ فَلاَ فَوْتَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: This is in this world.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: They will be swallowed up by the earth in al-Baydāʾ, and none of them will escape except one man, who will tell the people the news of his companions.
Qatāda said: This is in this world, when they see the might of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Al-Ḥasan said: This is when they come out of their graves.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This verse is difficult.
The meaning according to the first view:
when they are terrified in this world as death or some other [form] of Allah's might descends upon them — as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَكَفَرْنَا بِمَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ. فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهُمْ إيِمَانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا﴾.
And the meaning according to al-Ḥasan's view: when they are terrified as they come out of their graves, there is no escape they can reach, no refuge and no place to flee.
As Qatāda said: ﴿ولاتَ حينَ مَنَاصِ﴾.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأُخِذُواْ مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾.
That is, near for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; that is, because wherever they are, they are near to Allah and not far from Him.
And it is said: And if [you could see] the unbelievers when they are terrified on the Day of Resurrection, [taken] from a near place, that is, from Hell; they were seized and flung into it. «[Translator's note: the text reads ولو الكفارَ, apparently for ولو ترى الكفارَ "and if you could see the unbelievers".]»

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِهِ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ مِن مَّكَانِ بَعِيدٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَقَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِهِ﴾, that is, in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
[And Qatāda said]: That is, in Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
﴿وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ مِن مَّكَانِ بَعِيدٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Abū Mālik said: That is, repentance.
Mujāhid said: ﴿ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ﴾ is reaching for (al-tanāwul).
Qatāda said: ﴿ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ﴾ is reaching for repentance.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the clearest of them. One says ناشَ يَنُوشُ when one reaches for something; and the grammarians recited:
* "فهي تَنُوشُ الحَوْضَ نَوْشَاً مِنْ عَلاَ" * (so she reaches for the trough, taking from above)
And one says تَنَاوشَ القَوْمُ when people reach at one another without coming fully close.
The meaning is: and whence can they have repentance from a far place?
That is, the acceptance of repentance is far from it.
The Kufans read ﴿التَّنَاؤُشُ﴾ with hamza. Some lexicographers rejected it, saying: because "النَّأْش" is distance; so how could it be: "and whence can they have distance from a far place"?
Abū Jaʿfar said: He «[Translator's note: or "it", i.e. the language]» allows that the wāw be changed to hamza because it carries a ḍamma, and it would then have the first meaning.
Abū Isḥāq narrated from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ﴾:
He said: The return [to the world]; they asked for it at a time when there is no return. «[Translator's note: the text reads سألوه بحين ردٍّ; rendered according to the apparent sense.]»
Mujāhid said: ﴿مِن مَّكَانِ بَعِيدٍ﴾: what is between the Hereafter and this world.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This comes back to the first [view].

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقَدْ كَـفَرُواْ بِهِ مِن قَـبْلُ وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾.
That is, they disbelieved in Muḥammad ﷺ in this world — [this being said] when their faith does not benefit them.
﴿وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, by conjecture. He said: They say: There is no resurrection, no Paradise and no Fire.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾:
their saying: He is a sorcerer, he is a soothsayer, he is a poet.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَحِيلَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: And a barrier was placed between them and faith when they saw the punishment — meaning: the acceptance of faith.
Mujāhid said: A barrier was placed between them and the splendour of this world and its pleasure, and their wealth and their children.
﴿كَمَا فُعِلَ بِأَشْيَاعِهِم مِّن قَبْلُ﴾: Mujāhid said: That is, with the unbelievers before them.
﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ فِي شَكٍّ مُّرِيبِ﴾: So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He punishes for doubt.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (يوم) an adverb (ẓarf), the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (اذكر); (جميعا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the third-person pronoun in (يحشرهم); (للملائكة) attached to (يقول); and (الهمزة) for interrogation; (إيّاكم) a detached pronoun in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi, the word governing it being (يعبدون).
The clause «(اذكر) يوم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يحشرهم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «يقول ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يحشرهم.
The clause «هؤلاء ... كانوا» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «كانوا يعبدون..» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هؤلاء).
The clause «يعبدون ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كانوا.

safi-cedvel:41-44.t:
* I'rab:
(سبحانك) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, accusative; (من دونهم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first-person pronoun in وليّنا [Note: The muḍāf ilayhi here is governed by the muḍāf, so it is its object; hence a ḥāl from it is permissible.]; (بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (بهم) attached to (مؤمنون).
The clause «قالوا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحانك..» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «أنت وليّنا ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «كانوا يعبدون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعبدون الجنّ ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كانوا..
The clause «أكثرهم بهم مؤمنون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or causal (taʿlīliyya) —
(42) (الفاء) a conjunction; (اليوم) an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative, attached to the negated (يملك); (لا) negative; (لبعض) attached to (يملك) by its being made to imply (taḍmīn) the meaning of "to present/offer" (يقدّم) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from (نفعا).]; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation; (للذين) attached to (نقول); (التي) a relative noun in the position of genitive as naʿt (adjective) of النار; (بها) attached to (تكذّبون).
The clause «لا يملك بعضكم..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كانوا ...
The clause «نقول ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا يملك.
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ذوقوا ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «كنتم بها تكذّبون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «تكذّبون..» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كنتم.
(43) (الواو) resumptive; (عليهم) attached to (تتلى); (آياتنا) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (بيّنات) a ḥāl, accusative, from آياتنا; (ما) negative, inoperative (muhmala); (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (رجل) khabar of هذا, nominative; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle; (عمّا) attached to (يصدّكم); and the noun (ism) of (كان) is a pronoun necessarily latent (mustatir), referring to (آباؤكم), so in the speech there is tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one word).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يصدّكم..) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being يريد.
(ما هذا إلّا إفك) like ما هذا إلّا رجل; (مفترى) naʿt of إفك, nominative; (للحقّ) attached to (قال) by its being made to imply the meaning of a verb that is made transitive by lām [Note: Or it has the sense of (في), i.e. they said concerning the truth, i.e. concerning its matter..]; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when" (حين), implying the sense of condition, attached to the implied apodosis; (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction; (سحر) khabar of هذا, nominative.
The clause «تتلى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «قالوا....» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ما هذا إلّا رجل ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «يريد ...» is in the position of nominative as naʿt of رجل.
The clause «يصدّكم..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «كان يعبد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يعبد آباؤكم ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كان.
The clause «قالوا ... (the second)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالوا (the first).
The clause «ما هذا إلا إفك..» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «قال الذين....» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالوا.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «جاءهم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. when the truth came to them, those who disbelieved said ...
The clause «إن هذا إلّا سحر ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
(44) (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (كتب) genitive in form, accusative in position, the second mafʿūl bihi; (ما) like the first; (إليهم) attached to (أرسلنا); (قبلك) an adverb, accusative, attached to (أرسلنا); (نذير) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أرسلنا.
The clause «ما آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يدرسونها ...» is in the position of genitive — or accusative — as naʿt of كتب.
The clause «أرسلنا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما آتيناهم.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (al-takrīr): in the words of the Exalted «وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ».
In the repetition of the verb, namely their saying, in the explicit mention of the disbelievers, in what the two lāms carry of pointing to those who said it and to what it was said about, and in what «لما» carries of haste in pronouncing this false statement decisively, there is a great condemnation of it and an eloquent expression of astonishment at it. This is to indicate the extent of the displeasure with them, contempt for their worth, and astonishment at the relapse of their minds, their recoiling from the truth and their effacing of its landmarks.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (من قبلهم) attached to an omitted [element], the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun الذين; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) negative, and the second is a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the second object of the verb آتيناهم is omitted; (الفاء) a conjunction in both places; (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كان; (نكير) the noun (ism) of كان, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted in observance of the verse-endings (fawāṣil) ...
The clause «كذّب الذين من قبلهم..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive [clause] [Note: In the previous verse (44).].
The clause «ما بلغوا ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: It may be parenthetical, and so have no grammatical position.].
The clause «آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «كذّبوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كذّب الذين ...
The clause «كان نكير ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied clause, i.e.: when they denied My messengers, My disapproval came to them through punishment, so how was My disapproval.. i.e.: My disapproval was in its proper place.

* Morphology:
(معشار): a noun meaning a tenth, or a tenth of a tenth; some said it is a word equivalent to a tenth of the ʿashīr — and the ʿashīr is a tenth of a tenth. Its pattern (wazn) is مفعال; of the number words on this pattern none remains except it and المرباع.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(بواحدة) attached to (أعظكم) by its being made to imply (taḍmīn) the meaning of أوصيكم; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (لله) attached to (تقوموا).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تقوموا) is in the position of genitive as badal (substitute) of واحدة [Note: Or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هي, and the clause is a naʿt of واحدة.
(2, 3) Or attached to an omitted naʿt of نذير.].
(مثنى) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the fāʿil (agent) of تقوموا; (تتفكّروا) accusative, conjoined to تقوموا; (ما) negative; (بصاحبكم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate); (جنّة) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (لكم) attached to the khabar نذير «2»; (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to نذير «3».
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّما أعظكم ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «تقوموا..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «تتفكّروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تقوموا..
The clause «ما بصاحبكم من جنّة..» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of reflection, suspended (muʿallaq) by the negation.
The clause «إن هو إلّا نذير ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Rhetoric:
Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): in the words of the Exalted «مَثْنى وَفُرادى».
A fine antithesis, brought to guard against standing up as a group, because in gathering together there is a confusion of thoughts and a blinding of insight, preventing contemplation and absorption in reflection; whereas their standing in pairs and singly allows them to think and to exercise deliberation, and if the truth becomes clear to the two, each individual inclines to exercising his own judgement.

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of accusative as a fronted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (سألتكم) in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (من أجر) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ما [Note: Or it is the tamyīz (specification) of (ما).]; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (لكم) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هو; (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (على الله) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أجري; (الواو) a conjunction; (على كلّ) attached to the khabar شهيد.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما سألتكم من أجر ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «هو لكم..» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «إن أجري إلّا على الله ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech, for explanation.
The clause «هو ... شهيد» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the last resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(بالحقّ) attached to (يقذف), and (الباء) is causal [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied object of يقذف, and (الباء) is of accompaniment (mulābasa).. It is also permissible that (الباء) be instrumental (istiʿāna), so it is attached to (يقذف), i.e.: He hurls the truth at falsehood; or (الباء) is redundant (zāʾida) and the verb is made to imply the meaning of "casts" or "sends", like His words ولا تلقوا بأيديكم.. or the verb is made to imply the meaning of "judges" and "decrees"..]; (علّام) a second khabar (predicate), nominative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ ربّي ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «يقذف ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction — or parenthetical — and the second is a conjunction; (ما) negative in both places; and the fāʿil (agent) of (يعيد) refers to الباطل.
The clause «قل..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جاء الحقّ ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «ما يبدئ الباطل ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause جاء الحقّ [Note: Or parenthetical if the words are not part of the object of speech; or [ما is] a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted.].
The clause «ما يعيد..» is conjoined to the clause ما يبدئ and takes its grammatical status.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in the words of the Exalted «وَما يُبْدِئُ الْباطِلُ وَما يُعِيدُ».
I.e. it has gone and vanished, so that no trace of it remains. It is taken from the perishing of a living being: when it perishes, there remains for it no originating — i.e. doing something a first time — and no repeating — i.e. doing it a second time — as one says: "he neither eats nor drinks", i.e. he is dead. So the speech is a metonymy for what has been mentioned, or a figurative usage (majāz) branching from the metonymy.

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(ضللت) in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (إنّما) the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (على نفسي) attached to (أضلّ); (اهتديت) like ضللت; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (إليّ) attached to (يوحي).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما يوحي..) is in the position of genitive by (الباء), attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), and the mubtadaʾ (subject) is implied, its implied form being اهتدائي.
The clause «قل....» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إن ضللت ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «إنّما أضلّ....» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «إن اهتديت ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause ضللت.
The clause «يوحي ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «(يوحي) ربّي (اهتدائي)» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the second condition, joined with al-fāʾ.
The clause «إنّه سميع ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or causal (taʿlīliyya) —

safi-cedvel:51-54.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (إذ) an adverb borrowed for the future, attached to (ترى) [Note: Because of the certainty of its occurrence..]; and the object of ترى is omitted, its implied form being "their state" (حالهم); (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya); (لا) the lā of generic negation; (فوت) the noun (ism) of lā, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa in the position of accusative, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "there is no escape for them"; (الواو) a conjunction; (من مكان) attached to (أخذوا ...).
The clause «ترى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "you would have seen a tremendous matter"..
The clause «فزعوا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «لا فوت (لهم)..» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «أخذوا ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause فزعوا.
