His saying: «غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ»: mubtadaʾ and khabar. A muḍāf must be omitted, that is: "its morning journey is a month's journey" or "the extent of its morning journey is a month." If it were accusative it would be permissible, except that it has not been read thus, as far as I know.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «غَدْوَتُها ورَوْحَتُها», in the form of a single occurrence. The sentence is either resumptive or in the position of a ḥāl.

His saying: «مَنْ يَعْمَلُ»: it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar in the preceding preposition and its genitive noun, that is: "among the jinn are those who work"; or it may be in the position of accusative by an implied verb, that is: "and We subjected to him those who work." And «من الجنّ» is attached to this implied verb, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl or an explication. And «بإذن» is a ḥāl, that is: "made easy by the permission of his Lord." And al-idhn is a maṣdar annexed to its agent. It was also read «ومَنْ يُزِغْ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from azāgha, with its object omitted, that is: "and whoever makes himself deviate", that is, inclines it. And «مِنْ عذاب»: «مِنْ» marks the starting point or is partitive.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
And {يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ مَا يَشَآءُ}: it explains His saying «مَنْ يعمل». And «مِنْ مَحاريب» is an explication (bayān) of «ما يَشاء».

His saying: «كالجوابِ»: Ibn Kathīr read it retaining the yāʾ of «الجوابي» in continuation and in pause. Abū ʿAmr and Warsh retain it in continuation and drop it in pause. The rest drop it in both cases. And «كالجواب» is an adjective of «جِفان». «الجِفان» is the plural of «جَفْنَة». «الجوابي» is the plural of «جابِيَة», like ḍāriba and ḍawāribu. «الجابية» is a great basin, so named because water is gathered (yujbā) into it. Attributing the act to it is figurative, because it is gathered in it, as it is said khābiya for what is stored (yukhabbaʾu) in it. The poet said:

3724 - With bowls that visit our gathering, of fat slices of hump when the north wind blew; like basins, never ceasing to be filled, for the hospitality of guests or of the one at death's door (بجِفانٍ تَعْتَرِي نادِيَنا ... مِنْ سَدِيْفٍ حين هاجَ الصِّنَّبِرْ / كالجوابي لاتِني مُتْرَعَةً ... لِقِرى الأضيافِ أو للمحتضِرْ)

And al-Aʿshā said:

3725 - A bowl removed blame from the family of al-Muḥallaq, like a basin of the Iraqi stream, overflowing (نَفَى الذَّمَّ عن آلِ المُحَلَّقِ جَفْنَةٌ ... كجابِيَةِ السَّيْحِ العِراقيِّ تَفْهَقُ)

And al-Afwah said:

3726 - And cauldrons like firm hills, and bowls like basins, filled to the brim (وقُدُوْرٍ كالرُّبا راسِيَةٍ ... وجِفانٍ كالجَوابي مُتْرَعَهْ)

His saying: «شُكْراً»: several explanations are possible. The first: that it is a direct object, that is: "perform obedience". Prayer and the like are called thanks (shukr) because they fill its place. The second: that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of «اعْمَلوا», as if it were said: "give thanks, a thanks, by your work", or "work the work of gratitude". The third: that it is an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), that is: "for the sake of thanks". The fourth: that it is a maṣdar occupying the position of a ḥāl, that is: "thankfully". The fifth: that it is accusative by an implied verb of its own wording, its implied form being: "and give thanks, a thanks". The sixth: that it is an adjective of the maṣdar of «اعْمَلوا», its implied form being: "work a work of thanks", that is, possessing thanks.

His saying: «وقليلٌ»: an advanced khabar. And «من عبادِيْ» is an adjective of it, and «الشَّكورُ» is the mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {تَأْكُلُ}: either a ḥāl or resumptive. As for «مِنْسَأْتَه»: Ibn Dhakwān read it with a quiescent hamza; Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr with a pure alif; and the rest with a hamza carrying fatḥa.

«المِنْسَأَةُ» is the staff, a noun of instrument from nasaʾahu, that is, "he delayed it", like «المِكْسَحَة» and «المِكْنَسَة». With the hamza it is the dialect of Tamīm, and this was recited:

3727 - Is it on account of a rope, may you have no father, that you struck it with a staff, that your rope has dragged along ropes? (أمِنْ أَجْلِ حَبْلٍ لا أَباك ضَرَبْتَه ... بمِنْسَأَةٍ قد جَرَّ حَبْلُكَ أَحْبُلا)

With the alif it is the dialect of the Hijaz. And this was recited:

3728 - When you creep along on the staff from old age, then play and flirtation have drawn far from you (إذا دَبَبْتَ على المِنْساة مِنْ كِبَرٍ ... فقد تباعَدَ عنك اللهوُ والغَزَلُ)

As for the hamza with fatḥa, it is the original, because derivation indicates and attests to it, and the fatḥa is for the pattern mifʿala, like miknasa. As for its being quiescent, there are two explanations. The first: that he replaced the hamza with an alif, as Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr replaced it (this will come), then replaced this alif with a hamza in the dialect of those who say «العَأْلَم» and «الخَأْتَم», and the saying:

3729 - And Khindif is the head of this ʿaʾlam (the world) (وخِنْدِفٌ هامَةُ هذا العَأْلَمِ)

Ibn Mālik mentioned it. I do not know what led him to this: how can it be held that he fled from something and then returned to it? Moreover, they stated explicitly that when a hamza is substituted for an alif: if that alif has an origin, this hamza is given the vowel of the origin of the alif. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUṣfūr recited on this:

3730 - The ostriches of the Banū Ṣafwān fled, rushing off in a hurry ... (وَلَّى نَعامُ بني صفوانَ زَوْزَأَةً ...)

He said: the origin is «زَوْزاة», and the origin of this is «زَوْزَوَة»; when it was replaced from the alif by a hamza, he gave it the vowel of the wāw. Having known this, this alif should have been replaced by a hamza with fatḥa, because it is from a vowelled origin, namely the hamza with fatḥa, and so it would return to the first; and this is not said. The second: that he made the fatḥa quiescent for lightness, and the fatḥa has been made quiescent in places whose notice and attestations have been given. What makes it good here is that the hamza resembles the weak letters, and a weak letter finds a vowel heavy in general, even though the fatḥa is not heavy because of its lightness. They recited, for the quiescence of its hamza:

3731 - Slain by wine, he rose from his wineskin's tie, like the rising of the old man to his staff (صريعُ خَمْرٍ قام مِنْ وُكَاءَتِهْ ... كقَوْمَةِ الشيخ إلى مِنْسَأْتِهْ)

A group impugned this reading and attributed an error to its transmitter. They said: because the rule for lightening it is only easing it between the two (bayna bayna), and by this Ibn ʿĀmir and his two companions read, and so the transmitter supposed that they made it quiescent. Some also considered it weak on the ground that it requires quiescence of what is before the tāʾ of the feminine, while what is before it must carry fatḥa except an alif.

As for the reading of substitution, it was said: it is not according to the rule, meaning that it is not on the rule for lightening it. But this is rejected: it is the dialect of the Hijaz, established, so no regard is paid to one who impugned it. Abū ʿAmr said — and it suffices to cite him — "I do not pronounce the hamza, because I do not know any derivation for it; if it is among those not pronounced with hamza, I would have erred; and if it is pronounced with hamza, it is permissible for me to omit the hamza from what is pronounced with it." What Abū ʿAmr mentioned is the best that can be said about this and its like.

It was also read «مَنْسَأَتَه» with fatḥa on the mīm, along with a full hamza, with its replacement by an alif, and with its omission for lightness; and «مِنْسَاْءَتَه» on the pattern mifʿālatahu, as in their saying «مِيْضَأَة» and «مِيْضاءَة»; all of them are dialects.

Ibn Jubayr read «مِنْ سَأَتِه», separating «مِنْ» and making it a preposition, and making «سَأَتِه» genitive by it. «السَّأَة» and «السِّئَة» here are the staff. Its origin is the upper and lower tip of the bow; it is said sāt al-qaws, like shāt, and siʾatuhā; so the staff was named thus by way of metaphor. The meaning: it was eating from the end of his staff. The reason for that, as in the exegesis, is that he leaned upon a green staff of carob wood, and a green staff, when leaned upon, usually becomes bent like a bow. «ساة» is faʿala and «سِئَة» is fiʿla, like qiḥa and qaḥa, with the lām of both omitted.

Ibn Jinnī said: "He called the staff sāʾa because it harms (tasūʾu), so it is falla, with the ʿayn omitted." I say: this requires the reading to be with a quiescent hamza, while what is transmitted is that this reading is with an explicit alif; but Abū al-Fatḥ may say: its origin is the hamza, but it was substituted.

His saying: «دابَّةُ الأرضِ»: there are two explanations. The clearer: that «الأرض» is this well-known earth, and what is meant by "the creature of the earth" is the termite (al-araḍa), a small creature that eats wood. The second: that «الأرض» is a maṣdar from your saying araḍat al-dābba al-khashaba taʾriḍuhā arḍan, that is, "it ate it". So it is as if it were said: "a creature of eating". It is said: araḍat al-dābba al-khashaba taʾriḍuhā arḍan, then ariḍat (with kasra) taʾraḍu (with fatḥa) araḍan (with fatḥa also), like "the weevils ate the teeth, they eat them (taʾkuluhā) akl, then they themselves were eaten (akilat) with kasra, taʾkalu with fatḥa, akalan with fatḥa". Similar also: jadaʿtu anfahu jadʿan so he is jadiʿa jadaʿan with fatḥa on the ʿayn of the maṣdar. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl read with fatḥa on the rāʾ, and it strengthens the maṣdar sense in the well-known reading. It was also said: «الأرضَ» with fatḥa is not a maṣdar but a plural of «أَرَضَة», and on this it falls under the annexation of the general to the specific, because the creature is more general than the termite and other creatures.

His saying: «فلمَّا خَرَّ»: the apparent view is that its agent is the pronoun of Sulaymān, peace be upon him. It was said: it returns to the door, because the creature ate it and it fell. It was also said: rather it ate the threshold of the door, which is the thing that falls (al-khārra). That is reported in the exegesis, and it ought not to be sound, since the construction would then have been «خرَّتْ» with the tāʾ of the feminine. And:

3732 - ... ... it sprouted its sprouting (... أَبْقَل إبْقالَها)

is a necessity or a rarity. Interpreting it in the sense of the stick (ʿūd) is rarer still.

His saying: «تَبَيَّنَتْ»: the majority read it in the active, attributed to the jinn. There are several interpretations. The first: that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "the matter of the jinn became clear", that is, appeared and was evident. And «تبيَّن» comes as intransitive in the sense of bāna, as in the saying:

3733 - It became clear to me that shortness is humiliation, and that the mighty among men are the tall ones (تَبَيَّنَ لي أنَّ القَماءَةَ ذِلَّةٌ ... وأنَّ أَعِزَّاءَ الرجالِ طِيالُها)

When the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, and it was one of those whose verb may take the feminine, the sign of the feminine was attached. And His saying {أَن لَّوْ كَانُواْ}, interpreted as a maṣdar, is nominative as a badal of «الجنُّ». The meaning: "it became clear that, had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the punishment", that is, their ignorance appeared. The second: that «تبيَّن» is also in the sense of bāna and ẓahara, and «الجنُّ» is the agent. There is no need to omit a muḍāf, and {أَن لَّوْ كَانُواْ} is a badal as its explanation was given earlier. The meaning: "the jinn's ignorance became clear to people", because they used to make people suppose that (they knew the unseen), as you say: "bāna Zayd, his ignorance". The third: that «تَبَيَّن» here is transitive in the sense of "perceived and knew". In that case what is meant by "the jinn" is their weak ones, and by the pronoun in «كانوا» their great ones and rebels, and {أَن لَّوْ كَانُواْ} is the direct object. That is because the rebels and chiefs among the jinn used to make their weak ones suppose that they knew the unseen. When Sulaymān, peace be upon him, fell dead, they remained after him a year at work; the lowly among the jinn perceived that, if their chiefs had known the unseen as they claimed, they would not have remained in the punishment. Among the occurrences of «تَبَيَّن» as transitive in the sense of "perceived" is the saying:

3734 - O Fāṭima, I am dying, so perceive it, and do not be distressed; all creatures die (أفاطِمُ إنِّي مَيِّتٌ فَتَبَيَّني ... ولا تَجْزَعي كلُّ الأنامِ يموتُ)

that is: perceive that.

In the book of Abū Jaʿfar there is something requiring that some read «الجنَّ» accusative, and it is clear, that is: "mankind perceived the jinn", and {أَن لَّوْ كَانُواْ} is likewise a badal of «الجن». Ibn ʿAbbās and Yaʿqūb read «تُبُيِّنَتِ الجنّ» in the passive, and it supports what al-Naḥḥās transmitted. There are many readings in the verse that I have passed over because they contradict the written text of the Quran.

And «أن» in {أَن لَّوْ كَانُواْ}: the apparent view is that it is a maṣdar particle, lightened from the heavy one, its subject being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and «لو» separates it from its verbal predicate. The verification of that has been given, as in His saying {وَأَلَّوِ استقاموا} [al-Jinn: 16] and {أَن لَّوْ نَشَآءُ أَصَبْنَاهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 100].

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Sībawayh held that «أَنْ» has no position in iʿrāb; it only announces the answer to what is treated as an oath, from a verb whose meaning is verification and certainty, because these verbs, such as 'I verified', 'I was certain', 'I knew' and the like, take the place of an oath; so «ما لَبِثُوا» is the answer to the oath, not the answer to «لو», and according to the first views it is its answer." I say: the apparent sense of this is that it is redundant, because they stated that its redundancy before «لو» within the scope of an oath is regular. People differ: is the answer for the wāw (of «لو») or for the oath? What analogy requires is that the earlier of the two be answered, as in its combination with an explicit condition, so long as neither is preceded by something that takes a predicate, as its explanation was given earlier. The discussion and the readings of Saba' have been given in Sūrat al-Naml.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {مَسْكَنِهِمْ}: Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read «مَسْكَنِهم» with fatḥa on the kāf in the singular; al-Kisāʾī likewise, except that he put kasra on the kāf; the rest read «مَساكِنِهم» in the plural. As for the singular, it is because there is no ambiguity, as what is meant is the plural, as in the saying:

3735 - Eat in part of your belly and you will be chaste ... (كُلوا في بَعْضِ بَطْنِكُمُ تَعِفُّوا ...)

The fatḥa is the rule, because whenever the ʿayn of the imperfect of the verb has ḍamma or fatḥa, the mafʿal (form) from it, for time, place and maṣdar, comes with fatḥa, while the kasra is heard, not on the rule. Abū al-Ḥasan said: "The kasra on the kāf is a widespread dialect, the dialect of people today, and the kasra is the dialect of the Hijaz." al-Farrāʾ said: "It is a Yemeni dialect, eloquent." And «مَسْكَنِهِمْ» may be meant as the place, or may be meant as the maṣdar, that is, dwelling (al-suknā). Some preferred the second; he said: because the maṣdar covers all, so there is no putting of a singular in the place of a plural, unlike the first, where there is the putting of a singular in the place of a plural as I explained; but Sībawayh refuses this except of necessity, as in the saying:

3736 - ... the skin of buffaloes has bitten their necks (... قد عضَّ أعناقَهم جِلْدُ الجَواميسِ)

that is, skins. As for the plural, it is the apparent view, because each one has a dwelling. In the Quranic copies it is written without an alif after the kāf, and so it permits the readings mentioned.

His saying: «جَنَّتان»: there are three explanations: nominative as a badal of «آيةٌ», with a dual substituted for a singular, because this singular is true of this dual. This was given in His saying {وَجَعَلْنَا ابن مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً}. The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya considered the first weak without explaining it. Its weakness does not appear; rather, its strength; it is as if he supposed them to differ in singular and dual, and for that reason the badal was weak in his view. Allah knows best. The third — and Ibn ʿAṭiyya leaned to it — that «جَنَّتان» is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is {عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ}. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected it as a mubtadaʾ that is indefinite without a justification. He excused it: it may be held that an adjective is omitted, that is, "two gardens for them" or "two great gardens" [if] what he went for is sound.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «جَنَّتَيْن» with a yāʾ, accusative, as the khabar of kāna, with «آية» as its subject. If it is said: the subject of kāna is like a mubtadaʾ, and there is no justification for beginning with it unless it is made the subject of kāna. The answer: it is specified by the ḥāl advanced before it, which was originally its adjective. Do you not see that if «لسبأ» were delayed, it would be an adjective of «آيةٌ» in this reading?

His saying: «عن يمينٍ»: either an adjective of «جَنَّتان», or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "the two are on the right".

His saying: «كُلُوا»: by implying a saying, that is: "Allah said", or "the angel said".

His saying: «بَلْدَةٌ»: that is: "your land is a good land, and your Lord is a Forgiving Lord." Ruways read «بَلْدَة ورَب» accusative, for praise, or "dwell and worship". Abū al-Baqāʾ made it a direct object governed by «اشكروا», and there is a point to consider in it, since the implied form would become: "give thanks to your Lord, a Forgiving Lord."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {سَيْلَ العرم}: there are several explanations. The first: that it is of the type of annexing the described to its attribute, in origin, since the original is «السَّيْلُ العَرِمُ». «العَرِمُ» is the severe. Its origin is from ʿarāma, which is fierceness and hardness. It is said ʿarima so-and-so, so he is ʿārim and ʿarim. The ʿurām (tumult) of an army is from it. The second: that it is of the type of omitting the described and putting its attribute in its place; its implied form being: "so We sent upon them the flood of the severe rain", or "of the severe rat (al-juradh)", that is, the severe, the abundant. The third: that «العَرِمَ» is a name for the structure that is made as a dam. And it was recited:

3737 - Of Saba', the dwellers of Maʾrib, when they built the ʿarim in front of its flood (مِنْ سبأ الحاضرينَ مَأْرِبَ إذْ ... يَبْنُون مِنْ دونِ سَيْلِه العَرِما)

that is, the strong structure. The fourth: that «العَرِمَ» is a name for the valley in which the water itself was. The fifth: that it is a name for the juradh, which is the mouse. It was said: it is the mole-rat (al-khuld). It was annexed to it because it was the cause, since it is related in the exegesis that it gnawed the dam until it opened upon them and they were drowned by it. According to these last three views the iḍāfa is a sound, defining iḍāfa, like "Zayd's boy", that is: the flood of the structure, or the flood of such-and-such valley, or the flood of the rat. These are the ones the Arabs took as a proverb for dispersal, so they said: "They scattered like the hands of Saba' (aydī Saba' and ayādī Saba')."

His saying: «بجنَّتَيْهم جَنَّتَيْن»: it has already been given in al-Baqara that the one made genitive by the bāʾ is the one that goes out, and the accusative one is the one that enters; for this reason one who said among the jurists "if he replaces a ḍād with a ẓāʾ, his prayer is invalid" erred; rather, the correct form is to say "a ẓāʾ for a ḍād".

His saying: «أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ»: Abū ʿAmr read it with «أُكُل» annexed to «خَمْط». The rest read it with tanwīn, not annexed. It has already been given in al-Baqara that Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans put ḍamma on the kāf of «أكل» when it is not annexed to a feminine pronoun, and that Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr make it quiescent, with a detail given there. So the readers here are in three ranks. The first, Abū ʿAmr: «أُكُلِ خَمْط», with ḍamma on the kāf of «أُكُلٍ» annexed to «خَمْطٍ». The second, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr: quiescence of its kāf and tanwīn. The third, the rest: ḍamma on its kāf and tanwīn. One who annexes makes «الأكل» mean the fruit and produce. «الخَمْط», it was said, is the arāk tree. It was said: every thorny tree. It was said: every plant with a bitter taste. It was said: a tree with fruit resembling poppy that is not of benefit.

His saying: {وَأَثْلٍ وَشَيْءٍ مِّن سِدْرٍ}: both are conjoined to «أُكُل», not to «خَمْط», because «الخَمْط» has no fruit. Makkī said: "Since it is not permissible that «الخمط» be an adjective of «الأكل», because «الخمط» is the name of a specific tree, nor a badal, because it is not the first nor part of it, and the fruit and produce are of the tree, it was annexed on the implication of «مِنْ», like your saying 'this is a garment of silk'." And one who gives tanwīn makes «خَمْطاً» and what follows either an adjective of «أُكُل».

al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or the fruit was described by the khamṭ, as if it were said: 'possessors of a bitter fruit'." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "Describing by nouns is not regular, though some has occurred, as in their saying: 'I passed by a tract of all ʿarfaj'." The second: a badal of «أُكُل». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "He made khamṭ a fruit because of its adjacency to it and its being its cause." However, al-Fārisī rejected its being a badal; he said: "because the khamṭ is not the fruit itself." Abū al-Baqāʾ's answer has been given. Some answered for him — and it is drawn from the words of al-Zamakhsharī — that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "possessors of a fruit, the fruit of khamṭ." He said: the omitted one is in reality the first. I say: it is good in meaning. The third: that it is ʿaṭf bayān, and Abū ʿAlī made it the best in the chapter. He said: "It is as if he explained that the fruit is this tree." However, the Basrans do not allow ʿaṭf bayān with indefinite nouns, and restrict it to definite ones.

His saying: «قليلٍ»: an adjective of «سِدْر». It was also said: an adjective of «أُكل». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be an adjective of «خَمْطٍ وأَثْلٍ وسِدْرٍ»." It was also read «وأَثْلاً وشَيْئاً» accusative for both, conjoined to «جَنَّتَيْن». «الأَثْل» is the tamarisk tree, or what resembles it. «السِّدر» is of two kinds: a lote tree whose fruit is astringent, not eaten, and whose leaves are not used in washing, and this is the straying one (al-ḍāll); and a lote tree whose fruit is eaten, which is the nabq, and whose leaves are used in washing. What the verse intends is the first.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {وَهَلْ نجازي}: al-Akhawān and Ḥafṣ read «نُجازي» with the nūn of majesty and kasra on the zāy, that is "We". «إلاَّ الكَفورَ» is a direct object. The rest read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the zāy, in the passive; «إلاَّ الكفورُ» is nominative as the one whose agent is not named. Muslim ibn Jundab read «يُجْزَى» in the passive, «إلاَّ الكفورُ» nominative as stated. It was also read «يَجْزِي» in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted, and «الكفورَ» accusative as direct object.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {رَبَّنَا}: the majority read it accusative as a vocative. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Hishām read «بَعِّدْ» with a shadda on the ʿayn, a verb of request. The rest read «باعِدْ», also a request, from the form mufāʿala in the sense of the triliteral verb. Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «بَعُدَ» with ḍamma on the ʿayn, as a past verb. The agent is the journeying (al-masīr), that is: "the journey became distant"; and «بَيْنَ» is an adverb. Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan likewise, except that he put ḍamma on the nūn of «بين», making it the agent of «بَعُدَ», which removed it from being an adverb, like the reading «تَقَطَّع بينكُم» in the nominative. The meaning according to the reading that includes a request: they were insolent and ungrateful; for that reason they asked for distance in their journeys. And according to the reading that includes a past report, it is a complaint about the distance of the journeys, which they had also asked for.

A large group read, including Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid, «ربُّنا» nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «بَعِّدْ» with a shadda on the ʿayn as a past verb, its khabar. Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb read likewise, except that it is «باعَدَ» with an alif. The meaning according to this reading: a complaint about the distance of their journeys, despite their nearness and closeness, out of obstinacy on their part.

It was also read «بُوعِدَ» in the passive. When you make «بينَ» accusative after a transitive verb from this root in one of these readings, whether imperative or past, the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) made it accusative as a direct object, not an adverb. He said: "Do you not see how, in the reading of one who made it nominative, he made it a noun?" I say: leaving it as an adverb is preferable, with the object omitted, its implied form being: "make the travelling between our journeys distant." This is indicated by the reading «بَعُدَ» with ḍamma on the ʿayn and «بينَ» accusative: just as the agent is implied here, namely the pronoun of the travelling, so «بينَ» is left here on its basic status and the travelling is intended. This is preferable, because omission of the object is very frequent and undisputed, while taking a non-declinable adverb out of its adverbial status is much disputed. The verification of this and the excuse for the nominative of «بينكم» are mentioned in al-Anʿām.

The majority read «أَسْفارِنا» in the plural. Ibn Yaʿmar read «سَفَرِنا» in the singular.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {صَدَّقَ}: the Kufans read «صَدَّق» with a shadda on the dāl. The rest read it without the shadda. As for the first, «ظنَّه» is the direct object. The meaning: Iblīs's supposition went to something and it agreed, so he confirmed his supposition, by way of figurative and broad usage. Like it: "I belied my supposition and myself, and I confirmed them, and they confirmed me and belied me." It is an acceptable figurative usage. That is: he supposed something and it occurred. Its origin is from his saying «ولأُغْوِيَنَّهم» and «لأُضِلَّنَّهم» and other than that.

As for the second, «ظنَّه» is accusative as above, as a direct object, as in their saying: "I hit my supposition" and "I missed my supposition"; or as a maṣdar by an implied verb, that is: "he supposes his supposition"; or on the removal of the preposition, that is: "in his supposition". Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Zuhrī read «ظَنُّه» nominative and «إبليس» accusative, like the poet's saying:

3738 - If my supposition is true, and he is truthful to me ... (فإنْ يَكُ ظَنِّي صادِقاً وهو صادِقي ...)

he made his supposition true about what he supposed, figuratively and broadly. It was transmitted from Abū ʿAmr with both nominative, and it is clear: he made «ظنَّه» a badal of inclusion from «إبليس».

The apparent view is that the pronoun in «عليهم» returns to the people of Saba', and «إلاَّ فريقاً» is an exception from the agent of «اتبعوه», and «من المؤمنين» is an adjective of «فريقاً». And «مِنْ» is explicative, not partitive, lest the meaning be corrupted, since it would follow that some of those who believed followed Iblīs.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ لِنَعْلَمَ}: a complete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the general causes, its implied form being: "he had no domination over them for any reason at all except this, which is to distinguish the one who holds the truth from the one in doubt."

His saying: «منها»: attached to an omitted element in the sense of explication, that is: "I mean from it and because of it". It was said: «مِنْ» has the sense of "in". It was also said: it is a ḥāl from «شك». And His saying «مَنْ يؤمِنُ»: two explanations are possible for «مَنْ». The first: that it is interrogative, filling the place of the two objects of "knowing". Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it thus, and it is not apparent, because the meaning is: "except that We distinguish and make plain to people who believes from who does not believe", and He expressed its opposite by His saying {مِمَّنْ هُوَ مِنْهَا فِي شَكٍّ}, because it is one of its results and concomitants. The second: that it is a relative noun, and this is the apparent view, according to the explanation given earlier.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ (١))
His saying (فِي الْآخِرَةِ): it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) governed by «الْحَمْدُ» or by the adverbial phrase [لَهُ]; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الْحَمْدُ), governed by the adverbial phrase.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا وَهُوَ الرَّحِيمُ الْغَفُورُ (٢))
His saying (يَعْلَمُ): it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). It is also said: it is a corroborative ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida).

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَأْتِينَا السَّاعَةُ قُلْ بَلَى وَرَبِّي لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا أَصْغَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا أَكْبَرُ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ (٣))
His saying (عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ): it is read in the nominative (عَالِمُ), i.e. "He is the Knower" (هُوَ عَالِمُ); it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being (لَا يَعْزُبُ). And in the genitive, as a naʿt (adjective) of رَبِّي, or as a badal (substitute).
His saying (وَلَا أَصْغَرَ): in the genitive (with fatḥa, as a diptote) by conjunction with ذَرَّةٍ, and in the nominative by conjunction with مِثْقَالُ.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ (٤))
His saying (لِيَجْزِيَ): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the meaning of «لَا يَعْزُبُ»; it is as if He said: "He keeps count of that so that He may recompense".

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ سَعَوْا فِي آيَاتِنَا مُعَاجِزِينَ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٍ (٥))
His saying (مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ): it is read in the genitive (أَلِيمٍ) as a naʿt (adjective) of رِجْزٍ, and in the nominative (أَلِيمٌ) as a naʿt of عَذَابٌ. And الرِّجْزُ is punishment in general.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَرَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ هُوَ الْحَقَّ وَيَهْدِي إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ (٦))
His saying (وَيَرَى): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to لِيَجْزِيَ. It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
And (الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ) is the first object, and «الْحَقَّ» the second object; and «هُوَ» is a separating pronoun (faṣl).
It has also been read الْحَقُّ in the nominative, as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
The fāʿil (agent) of «يَهْدِي» is the pronoun of الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ; it may also be the pronoun of the name of Allah.
It [يَهْدِي] may also be conjoined to the position of الْحَقَّ, with «أَنْ» omitted. And it may be in the position of an [active] participle (fāʿil), i.e. "and they see it as true and guiding" (وَيَرَوْهُ حَقًّا وَهَادِيًا).

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى رَجُلٍ يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ أَفْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ بَلِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ فِي الْعَذَابِ وَالضَّلَالِ الْبَعِيدِ (٨))
His saying (إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ): what governs «إِذَا» is what the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ indicates, i.e. "when you have been torn apart you will be raised" (إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ بُعِثْتُمْ). يُنَبِّئُكُمْ does not govern it, because their being informed does not take place at the time of their being torn apart; nor does مُزِّقْتُمْ, because إِذَا is in genitive construct with it; nor «جَدِيدٍ», because what comes after إِنَّ does not govern what precedes it — though some allowed this in the case of adverbs (al-ẓurūf).
(أَفْتَرَى): the hamza is for interrogation, and the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) has been dropped, being dispensed with.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنْ نَشَأْ نَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضَ أَوْ نُسْقِطْ عَلَيْهِمْ كِسَفًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ (٩))
His saying (نَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ): pronouncing [the fāʾ] distinctly (al-iẓhār) is the original; assimilation (al-idghām) [of the fāʾ into the bāʾ] is permissible, because fāʾ and bāʾ are close [in articulation].

ukberi-tibyan:10-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا دَاوُدَ مِنَّا فَضْلًا يَا جِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ وَالطَّيْرَ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِيدَ (١٠) أَنِ اعْمَلْ سَابِغَاتٍ وَقَدِّرْ فِي السَّرْدِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا إِنِّي بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (١١))
His saying (يَاجِبَالُ): i.e. "and We said: O mountains". It may also be an explanation of الْفَضْل ("the bounty"); and likewise «وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ».
(وَالطَّيْرَ) in the accusative, on which there are four views. First: it is conjoined to the position of جِبَالُ. Second: the wāw has the meaning of "with" (مَعَ) [i.e. it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment)], and what the wāw connects it to is «أَوِّبِي», because it is put in the accusative only together with a verb. [Translator's note: the printed text reads وَالَّذِي أَوْ صِلَتُهُ الْوَاوُ, evidently a corruption of وَالَّذِي أَوْصَلَتْهُ الْوَاوُ; translated accordingly.] Third: that it is conjoined to «فَضْلًا», the implied form being "and the glorification of the birds" (وَتَسْبِيحَ الطَّيْرِ); al-Kisāʾī said this. Fourth: by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We subjected the birds to him" (وَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ الطَّيْرَ).
It is also read in the nominative (وَالطَّيْرُ), on which there are two views. First: it is conjoined to the wording of جِبَالُ. Second: to the pronoun in أَوِّبِي, the «مَعَ» [i.e. مَعَهُ] making its emphasis unnecessary.
His saying (أَنِ اعْمَلْ): أَنْ has the meaning of أَيْ ("that is"), i.e. "We commanded him: make …" (أَمَرْنَاهُ أَنِ اعْمَلْ).
It is also said: it is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).

ukberi-tibyan:12-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ الرِّيحَ غُدُوُّهَا شَهْرٌ وَرَوَاحُهَا شَهْرٌ وَأَسَلْنَا لَهُ عَيْنَ الْقِطْرِ وَمِنَ الْجِنِّ مَنْ يَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ وَمَنْ يَزِغْ مِنْهُمْ عَنْ أَمْرِنَا نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ السَّعِيرِ (١٢) يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ مَا يَشَاءُ مِنْ مَحَارِيبَ وَتَمَاثِيلَ وَجِفَانٍ كَالْجَوَابِ وَقُدُورٍ رَاسِيَاتٍ اعْمَلُوا آلَ دَاوُدَ شُكْرًا وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبَادِيَ الشَّكُورُ (١٣))
His saying (وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ الرِّيحَ): it is read in the accusative, i.e. "and We subjected" (وَسَخَّرْنَا). And in the nominative (الرِّيحُ), as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or on the basis that it is a fāʿil (agent) [of the adverbial phrase].
And (غُدُوُّهَا شَهْرٌ) is a clause in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الرِّيحِ»; the implied form is "the duration of its morning course", because الْغُدُوُّ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), not a time.
(مَنْ يَعْمَلُ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "and We subjected to him, of the jinn, a group that works"; or in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ or as a fāʿil, i.e. "and he had, of the jinn, a group that works".
And (آلَ دَاوُدَ): i.e. "O family [of David]", or "I mean the family of David".
And (شُكْرًا) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). It is also said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a work of thanks" (عَمَلًا شُكْرًا).
The implied form may also be "give thanks with thanks" (اشْكُرُوا شُكْرًا).

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا قَضَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ الْمَوْتَ مَا دَلَّهُمْ عَلَى مَوْتِهِ إِلَّا دَابَّةُ الْأَرْضِ تَأْكُلُ مِنْسَأَتَهُ فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ الْجِنُّ أَنْ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ الْغَيْبَ مَا لَبِثُوا فِي الْعَذَابِ الْمُهِينِ (١٤))
His saying (مِنْسَأَتَهُ): the original has the hamza, because it is from نَسَأْتُ النَّاقَةَ and other animals, when you drive them; الْمِنْسَأَةُ is the staff with which [animals] are driven. However, its hamza was changed into an alif for lightness.
It has been read among the anomalous readings (al-shādhdh) «مِنْ سَأَتِهِ», with kasra on the tāʾ, on the basis that «مِنْ» is a preposition. It has been said that its reader made a mistake. Ibn Jinnī said: the staff was called سَأَةٌ because it causes harm (تَسُوءُ); so it is on the pattern falatun, with the middle radical (ʿayn) omitted. There is far-fetchedness in this.
His saying (تَبَيَّنَتْ): with the agent named (active voice), the implied form being "the matter of the jinn became clear" (تَبَيَّنَ أَمْرُ الْجِنِّ).
And (أَنْ لَوْ كَانُوا) is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) of the implied «أَمْرُ»; because the meaning is "mankind came to see clearly the ignorance of the jinn".
It may also be in the position of the accusative, i.e. "the jinn came to see clearly their own ignorance".
It is also read (تُبُيِّنَتْ) with the agent unnamed (passive), and on the first view this is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ كَانَ لِسَبَأٍ فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ جَنَّتَانِ عَنْ يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ كُلُوا مِنْ رِزْقِ رَبِّكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ (١٥))
His saying (لِسَبَأٍ): this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Naml.
And (مَسَاكِنَ) is the plural of مَسْكَنٌ, with fatḥa and with kasra [on the kāf]; both mean the dwelling, the place of residing. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), in which case the singular has fatḥa, like الْمَقْعَدُ and الْمَطْلَعُ; and the place [noun] has kasra.
And (آيَةٌ) is the noun (ism) of كَانَ.
And (جَنَّتَانِ) is a badal (substitute) of it, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).
His saying (بَلْدَةٌ): i.e. "this is a land" (هَذِهِ بَلْدَةٌ).
(وَرَبٌّ): i.e. "and your Lord is a Lord …" (وَرَبُّكُمْ رَبٌّ), or "and you have a Lord" (وَلَكُمْ رَبٌّ).
It is read anomalously «بَلْدَةً وَرَبًّا» in the accusative, on the basis that it is the object of the thanksgiving.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَعْرَضُوا فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ الْعَرِمِ وَبَدَّلْنَاهُمْ بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَوَاتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ وَأَثْلٍ وَشَيْءٍ مِنْ سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ (١٦))
His saying (أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ): it is read with tanwīn (nunation); the implied form is "fruit — the fruit of khamṭ" (أُكُلٍ أُكُلِ خَمْطٍ), and the muḍāf was omitted, because الْخَمْطُ is a tree and الْأُكُلُ is fruit. It is also said: the implied form is "fruit possessing khamṭ" (أُكُلٍ ذِي خَمْطٍ). It is also said: it is a badal (substitute) of it, «خَمْطٍ» being made fruit because of its adjacency to it and its being its cause.
It is also read with genitive construct (أُكُلِ خَمْطٍ), and that is clear.
And (قَلِيلٍ) is a naʿt (adjective) of أُكُلٍ. It may also be a naʿt of خَمْطٍ, أَثْلٍ and سِدْرٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَالُوا رَبَّنَا بَاعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا وَظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ وَمَزَّقْنَاهُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ (١٩))
His saying (رَبَّنَا): it is read in the accusative as a vocative.
And «بَاعِدْ» [is also read] بَعِّدْ, and [it is read] in the form of the past. [Translator's note: the printed text reads بَعَّدَ, عَلَى لَفْظِ الْمَاضِي; the imperative بَعِّدْ is likely intended for the first, with the past-tense reading following.]
It is also read: رَبُّنَا, with «بَاعَدَ» and «بَعُدَ», as a statement.
And (مُمَزَّقٌ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) or a place.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ فَاتَّبَعُوهُ إِلَّا فَرِيقًا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٢٠))
His saying (صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ): with the lightened form (صَدَقَ), «إِبْلِيسُ» is its fāʿil (agent), and «ظَنَّهُ» is in the accusative as its object; as if he had thought something about them and promised himself it, and then made it come true.
It is also said: the implied form is "he was truthful in his opinion" (صَدَقَ فِي ظَنِّهِ); when the preposition was omitted, the verb reached [the noun] directly.
It is also read with shadda (صَدَّقَ) with this meaning.
It is also read «إِبْلِيسَ» in the accusative, as object, with ظَنُّهُ as agent; as in the saying of the poet:
فَإِنْ يَكُ ظَنِّي صَادِقًا وَهُوَ صَادِقِي
("If my opinion is true — and it has proved true to me …")
And it is read with both in the nominative, making the second a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِالْآخِرَةِ مِمَّنْ هُوَ مِنْهَا فِي شَكٍّ وَرَبُّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ (٢١))
His saying (مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ): it may have the meaning of الَّذِي ("the one who"), and so be in the accusative, governed by نَعْلَمَ; and it may be an interrogative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And (مِنْهَا): either by way of explanation (tabyīn), i.e. "for doubt of it", i.e. "because of it"; or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «شَكٍّ». It is also said: «مِنْ» has the meaning of فِي ("in/about").

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ حَتَّى إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ قَالُوا مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ (٢٣))
His saying (إِلَّا لِمَنْ أَذِنَ): the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to الشَّفَاعَةُ, because you say "I interceded for him" (شَفَعْتُ لَهُ); and it may be attached to تَنْفَعُ.
(فُزِّعَ) with shadda, with the agent unnamed (passive); what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is «عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ», and the meaning is "[fear] was removed from their hearts". It is also said: what is predicated of is an implied verbal notion indicated by the context, i.e. "the fear was put away".
It is also read with fatḥa (فَزَّعَ), with the agent named, i.e. "Allah removed [the fear]", i.e. lifted it from them.
It is also read فَرَّغَ, i.e. "emptied" (أَخْلَى).
It has been read anomalously «افْرَنْقَعَ», i.e. "dispersed"; reciting with it is not permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ مَنْ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ وَإِنَّا أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَى هُدًى أَوْ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ (٢٤))
His saying (أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ): it is conjoined to the noun of إِنَّ. As for the khabar (predicate), it must be [understood as] repeated, as in your saying إِنَّ زَيْدًا وَعَمْرًا قَائِمٌ ("Zayd and ʿAmr are standing"), the implied form being إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ وَإِنَّ عَمْرًا قَائِمٌ.
They differed over the khabar that is mentioned: some said it belongs to the first, and some said it belongs to the second. On this [first view] «لَعَلَى هُدًى» is the khabar of the first, and «أَوْ فِي ضَلَالٍ» is conjoined to it, with the khabar of the conjoined element omitted because the one mentioned indicates it.
Others reversed this. The discussion according to meaning is different from the iʿrāb, because the meaning is: "we are upon guidance without doubt, and you are in error without doubt"; but He blended it in the wording according to their custom in parallel cases, as in their saying: "May Allah disgrace the liar, whether of me or of you" (أَخْزَى اللَّهُ الْكَاذِبَ مِنِّي وَمِنْكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلَّا كَافَّةً لِلنَّاسِ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٢٨))
His saying (إِلَّا كَافَّةً): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object in «أَرْسَلْنَاكَ», and the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] is added for intensiveness (mubālagha).
And (لِلنَّاسِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, i.e. "We have sent you only as one who restrains (kāffa) people from disbelief and sins".
It is also said: it is a ḥāl of النَّاسِ; but that is weak according to most, because the possessor of the ḥāl is in the genitive. It is weak here from another angle as well: on this view the lām would have the meaning of إِلَى ("to"), since the meaning is "We sent you to the people"; it is also possible for the implied form to be "for the sake of the people" (مِنْ أَجْلِ النَّاسِ).

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لَكُمْ مِيعَادُ يَوْمٍ لَا تَسْتَأْخِرُونَ عَنْهُ سَاعَةً وَلَا تَسْتَقْدِمُونَ (٣٠))
His saying (مِيعَادُ يَوْمٍ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in genitive construct with the adverb of time (ẓarf).
The hāʾ in «عَنْهُ» may refer back to الْمِيعَادُ or to الْيَوْمُ; whichever of the two you make it refer to, the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of it.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ إِذْ تَأْمُرُونَنَا أَنْ نَكْفُرَ بِاللَّهِ وَنَجْعَلَ لَهُ أَنْدَادًا وَأَسَرُّوا النَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَغْلَالَ فِي أَعْنَاقِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (٣٣))
His saying (بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ): it is like مِيعَادُ يَوْمٍ.
It is also read with fatḥa on the kāf and shadda on the rāʾ (مَكَرُّ), the implied form being "rather, the recurrence of night and day upon us turned us away" (بَلْ صَدَّنَا كُرُورُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ عَلَيْنَا).
It is also read the same way but in the accusative (مَكَرَّ), on the implied form "for the duration of their recurrence" (مُدَّةَ كُرُورِهِمَا).

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُكُمْ بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِنْدَنَا زُلْفَى إِلَّا مَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ جَزَاءُ الضِّعْفِ بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَهُمْ فِي الْغُرُفَاتِ آمِنُونَ (٣٧))
His saying (زُلْفَى): a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the meaning, i.e. "brings you near with a nearness" (يُقَرِّبُكُمْ قُرْبَى).
(إِلَّا مَنْ آمَنَ): it may be in the position of the accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); it may be a joined (muttaṣil) exception, excepted from the object in «تُقَرِّبُكُمْ»; and it may be in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows it as the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ وَمَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ (٣٩))
His saying (وَمَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُ): there are two views on «مَا».
First: it is conditional, in the position of the accusative; the fāʾ [introduces] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «مِنْ شَيْءٍ» is an explanation (tabyīn).
Second: it has the meaning of الَّذِي ("that which"), in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows the fāʾ is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يَقُولُ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ أَهَؤُلَاءِ إِيَّاكُمْ كَانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ (٤٠))
His saying (أَهَؤُلَاءِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «إِيَّاكُمْ» is in the position of the accusative, governed by «يَعْبُدُونَ», and «يَعْبُدُونَ» is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ. This is evidence that the khabar of كَانَ may be placed before it, because what the khabar governs has the same status as the khabar itself.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَعِظُكُمْ بِوَاحِدَةٍ أَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ مَثْنَى وَفُرَادَى ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا مَا بِصَاحِبِكُمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ (٤٦))
His saying (أَنْ تَقُومُوا): it is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) of «وَاحِدَةٍ»; or of the nominative on the implied form "it is that you stand" (هِيَ أَنْ تَقُومُوا); or of the accusative on the implied form "I mean" (أَعْنِي).
And (تَتَفَكَّرُوا) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «تَقُومُوا».
And (مَا بِصَاحِبِكُمْ) is a negation.
(بَيْنَ يَدَيْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for نَذِيرٌ; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of نَذِيرٌ. And it is permissible for «لَكُمْ» to be a naʿt of نَذِيرٌ, in which case «بَيْنَ» is an adverb of the [notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, or another naʿt.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ (٤٨))
His saying (عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ): in the nominative, on the basis that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); or a second khabar; or a badal (substitute) of the pronoun in «يَقْذِفُ»; or a naʿt (adjective) according to the position [of the noun of إِنَّ].
And in the accusative (عَلَّامَ), as a naʿt of the noun of «إِنَّ», or by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean").

ukberi-tibyan:51-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذْ فَزِعُوا فَلَا فَوْتَ وَأُخِذُوا مِنْ مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ (٥١) وَقَالُوا آمَنَّا بِهِ وَأَنَّى لَهُمُ التَّنَاوُشُ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ وَقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ (٥٢))
His saying (فَلَا فَوْتَ): i.e. "there is no escape for them".
And (التَّنَاوُشُ), without hamza, is from نَاشَ يَنُوشُ, when one reaches for something. The meaning is: "Whence can they reach safety?!" It is also read with hamza (التَّنَاؤُشُ) because of the ḍamma on the wāw.
It is also said: it [the hamza] is radical, from نَأَشَهُ يَنْأَشُهُ, when one rescues him. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Sabaʾ
﷽
﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ ولَهُ الحَمْدُ في الآخِرَةِ﴾: Allah is the One praised in this world and the Hereafter. His being praised in the Hereafter is indicated by the words of the people of Paradise: ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي صَدَقَنا وعْدَهُ وأوْرَثَنا الأرْضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ الجَنَّةِ حَيْثُ نَشاءُ﴾ [al-Zumar: 74], that is: He has made us inherit the land of Paradise.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿يَعْلَمُ ما يَلِجُ في الأرْضِ وما يَخْرُجُ مِنها﴾, that is: what enters the earth and what comes out of it — what enters the earth of rain and other things, and what comes out of it of crops and other things. ﴿وَما يَنْـزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ وما يَعْرُجُ فِيها﴾: what ascends in it. One says: ”عَرِجَ، يَعْرُجُ“ when one ascends, and ”اَلْمَعارِجُ“ are the steps, from this. One also says: ”عَرِجَ، يَعْرِجُ“ when one becomes lame (dhā ʿaraj), and ”عَرَجَ، يَعْرُجُ“ when one limps from something that has befallen him. «[Translator's note: the source prints the ascending verb as ”عَرِجَ، يَعْرُجُ“; the usual form is ʿaraja, yaʿruju; it is translated as written.]»

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَأْتِينا السّاعَةُ﴾: the Hour in which creation is resurrected. The meaning is that they said: "We will not be resurrected." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿قُلْ بَلى ورَبِّي لَتَأْتِيَنَّكم عالِمِ الغَيْبِ لا يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ مِثْقالُ ذَرَّةٍ﴾, with the genitive in ”عالِمِ“, as an attribute (ṣifa) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is also read in the nominative, on two accounts. One of them is as mubtadaʾ (subject), the meaning being: "The Knower of the unseen — nothing escapes Him", so that ”لا يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ“ is the khabar (predicate) of ”عالِمُ الغَيْبِ“. And it is made nominative by way of praise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the meaning being: "He is the Knower of the unseen". The accusative is also permissible, though it has not been read, on the meaning: "Remember the Knower of the unseen". It is also read: ”عَلّامُ الغُيُوبِ“, and ”عَلّامَ الغَيْبِ“ is permissible. It is also read: ”لا يَعْزِبُ عَنْهُ“ with kasra on the zāy. One says: ”عَزَبَ عَنِّي، يَعْزُبُ، ويَعْزِبُ“ when something is hidden [from one].

zajjaj:4-4.t:
﴿لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: the lām has come in as a response to His words: ﴿قُلْ بَلى ورَبِّي لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 3], for recompense, that is: for the sake of recompense with reward and punishment.
His words: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ ورِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾: Allah has made clear that their recompense is forgiveness, which is the covering over of sins.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His words, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿والَّذِينَ سَعَوْا في آياتِنا مُعاجِزِينَ﴾: it is also read: ”مُعَجِّزِينَ“. ”مُعاجِزِينَ“ is in the sense of ”مُسابِقِينَ“ (racing to outdo). Whoever reads ”مُعَجِّزِينَ“, its meaning is that they hinder (yuʿajjizūna) those who believe in them, so it is in the sense of ”مُثَبِّطِينَ“ (holding back), and that is the meaning of their hindering those who believe in them.
His words: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم عَذابٌ مِن رِجْزٍ ألِيمٌ﴾: ”ألِيمٍ“ in the genitive is a naʿt (adjective) of al-zajz «[Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for al-rijz (”رِجْزٍ“)]», and ”ألِيمٌ“ [in the nominative] is a naʿt of al-ʿadhāb.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَيَرى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا العِلْمَ الَّذِي أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ هو الحَقَّ﴾: here [those given knowledge are] the scholars of the Jews who believed in the Prophet — upon him be peace —, among them Kaʿb al-Aḥbār and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām. That is: ”وَلِيَرى“ (and so that … may see); the position of ”يَرى“ is conjoined to His words: ”لِيَجْزِيَ“. ”اَلْحَقَّ“ is accusative, a khabar (predicate) of ”يَرى الَّذِينَ“ «[Translator's note: i.e. the second object of yarā]». ”هو“ here is a faṣl (separating pronoun) indicating that what follows it is not a naʿt (adjective); the Kufans call it al-ʿimād (the support). ”هو“ does not enter as an ʿimād except with a definite noun and what resembles it; we have explained that in what has gone before. The nominative is permissible in His words ”هو الحَقُّ“.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَلْ نَدُلُّكم عَلى رَجُلٍ﴾, the verse: this is the saying of the idolaters who do not believe in the resurrection; some of them say to others: "Shall we point you to Muḥammad, who claims that you will be resurrected after you have become bones, dust and crumbled remains?" In this verse there is a subtle point of Arabic, and we shall explain it, if Allah wills. ”إذا“ is in the position of the accusative through ”مُزِّقْتُمْ“, and ”جَدِيدٍ“ cannot govern it, because what comes after ”أنْ“ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the verse is إنَّ]» does not govern what precedes it. The interpretation is: "Shall we point you to a man who says to you that, when you are torn to pieces, you will be resurrected?" So ”إذا“ is in the position of the ”إنْ“ of condition (al-jazāʾ), governed by what follows it. Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm said:
إذا قَصُرَتْ أسْيافُنا كانَ وصْلُها ∗∗∗ خُطانا إلى أعْدائِنا فَنُضارِبْ
(When our swords fall short, their extension is our steps towards our enemies, and so we strike.)
The meaning is: "their extension will be"; the proof of that is the jussive of ”فَنُضارِبْ“. It may also be that what governs ”إذا“ is an implied (muḍmar) [verb], indicated by ”إنَّكم لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“, the meaning being: "Shall we point you to a man who informs you, saying to you: when you are torn to pieces you will be resurrected — you will be in a new creation?", just as they said: ﴿أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا وعِظامًا أإنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 16], where ”إذا“ may be accusative through a verb indicated by ”إنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ“. ”أنَّكم لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“ with fatḥa is not permissible, because when the lām comes, nothing but kasra of ”إنَّ“ is permissible.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى ما بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ وما خَلْفَهم مِنَ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: "Have they not reflected and known that the One who created the heaven and the earth is able to resurrect them, and able to make the earth swallow them, or to make the heaven fall upon them in fragments?"
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآيَةً لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ﴾, that is: in that there is a sign that shows whoever turns to Allah, returns to Him and reflects on what He has created, that He is able to give life to the dead.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ مِنّا فَضْلا يا جِبالُ أوِّبِي مَعَهُ والطَّيْرَ﴾: the meaning is: “And We said: O mountains, repeat [praise] with him. It is also read: “ أُوبِي مَعَهُ ”, on the meaning “ return to glorification with him whenever he returns to it ”. Whoever reads: “ أوِّبِي مَعَهُ ”, its meaning is: echo with him; one says: “ آبَ، يَؤُوبُ ” when one returns. The meaning of “ رَجِّعِي مَعَهُ ” is: glorify with him, and echo the glorification with him. “ والطَّيْرَ ” and “ والطَّيْرُ ”: the nominative is on two accounts. One of them is that it be conjoined (nasaq) to what is in “ أوِّبِي ” [i.e. its pronoun]; the meaning is: “ O mountains, echo the glorification, you and the birds ”. It may also be nominative as a badal (substitute); the meaning is: “ O mountains, and O birds, echo with him ”. The accusative is on three accounts: that it be conjoined to His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ مِنّا فَضْلا﴾ ﴿والطَّيْرَ﴾, that is: and We subjected the birds to him — Abū ʿUbayda related that from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ. It may be accusative by the vocative (al-nidāʾ); the meaning is: “ O mountains, echo with him, and the birds ”, as though He said: “ We called the mountains and the birds ”, so “ اَلطَّيْرَ ” is conjoined to the position of “ اَلْجِبالَ ” in origin; every one addressed (munādā) — according to all the Basrans — is in the position of the accusative. We have explained the state of the vocative with ḍamma, and that the definite one is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma. And it may be that “ والطَّيْرَ ” is accusative on the meaning of “ مَعَ ” (with), as you say: “ قُمْتُ وزَيْدًا ”, that is: “ I stood with Zayd ”; so the meaning is: “ echo with him and with the birds ".

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَألَنّا لَهُ الحَدِيدَ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 10] ﴿أنِ اعْمَلْ سابِغاتٍ﴾, that is: We made it soft. The first to make coats of mail was David; before that, the iron with which people protected themselves was only pieces of iron, like these breastplates (al-jawāshin).
”أنْ“ here is in the sense of explanation (al-tafsīr), as though it were said: ”وَألَنّا لَهُ الحَدِيدَ أيِ اعْمَلَ سابِغاتٍ“ (and We softened iron for him, that is: make full coats of mail), in the sense of "We said to him: make full coats of mail". It may also be in the sense of: "so that he might make full coats of mail", with ”أنْ“ joined to the wording of the imperative. Like this in speech is ”أرْسَلَ إلَيْهِ أنْ قُمْ إلَيَّ“ (he sent to him: stand and come to me), that is: he said: "Go to so-and-so"; and it may be in the sense of: "send to him that he should go to so-and-so". The meaning of ”سابِغاتٍ“ is: ample coats of mail; He mentioned the attribute because it indicates what is qualified. The meaning of ”اَلسّابِغُ“ is that which covers everything it is on, so that it is more than enough. ﴿وَقَدِّرْ في السَّرْدِ﴾: ”اَلسَّرْدُ“ in the language is bringing one thing up to another so that you produce it in order, one part following another in succession; from it is ”سَرَدَ فُلانٌ الحَدِيثَ“ (so-and-so narrated the account in sequence). It is said in the exegesis: ”اَلسَّرْدُ“ is riveting, covering and forming the rings. It is also said: it is that he should not make the rivet thick and the hole narrow, nor make the rivet thin and the hole wide, so that it rattles, comes loose and breaks. ”قَدِّرْ في ذَلِكَ“, that is: make it in due proportion and according to need. What has come in the exegesis does not depart from the language, because riveting is your bringing one end of the ring up to its other end. Sībawayh claimed that the saying of the Arabs ”رَجُلٌ سَرَنْدِيٌّ“ is derived from ”اَلسَّرْدُ“, because its meaning is "the bold one"; he said: "the bold one" is he who goes straight ahead.
The explanation of ﴿وَألَنّا لَهُ الحَدِيدَ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 10] is: We made it soft like threads, yielding to him, so that he made the coats of mail.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ﴾: the accusative in ”اَلرِّيحَ“ is the [preferred] way, and it is the reading of most readers, on the meaning: "and We subjected the wind to Solomon". The nominative is also permissible: ”وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحُ غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ“, the nominative being on the meaning: "the wind was established for him", and in meaning it comes back to the sense of "We subjected the wind", just as when you say: ”لِلَّهِ الحَمْدُ“, its interpretation is: "praise is established for Allah", and it comes back to the meaning: "I praise Allah with praise".
His words: ﴿غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ ورَواحُها شَهْرٌ﴾, that is: its morning course is a month's journey, and likewise its evening course. Solomon would sit on his throne together with his companions, and the wind would carry them in the morning a month's journey and carry them in the evening a month's journey. ﴿وَأسَلْنا لَهُ عَيْنَ القِطْرِ﴾: ”اَلْقِطْرُ“ is copper, which is brass (al-ṣufr); it was melted from that time on, and before Solomon it did not melt. ﴿وَمِنَ الجِنِّ مَن يَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾: the position of ”مَن“ is accusative; the meaning is: "We subjected to him, of the jinn, those who work". The position of ”مَن“ may also be nominative, the meaning being: "among what We gave him, of the jinn, are those who work before him by the permission of his Lord", that is: by the command of his Lord. ﴿وَمَن يَزِغْ مِنهم عَنْ أمْرِنا﴾, that is: "whoever deviates".

zajjaj:13-13.t:
Then He made clear what they used to do before him, saying: ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ ما يَشاءُ مِن مَحارِيبَ وتَماثِيلَ﴾: ”اَلْمِحْرابُ“ is that in which one prays, and the most honoured place in a dwelling and in a house is called ”اَلْمِحْرابُ“. ﴿وَجِفانٍ كالجَوابِ﴾: most readers pause without a yāʾ. The original was to pause with the yāʾ, except that the kasra stands in for it. Without the alif and lām, the pause on it is without a yāʾ — you say: ”هَذِهِ جَوابٍ“ — and then the alif and lām were added, and the word was left as it was before they were added. ”اَلْجَوابِي“ is the plural of ”جابِيَةٌ“, and ”اَلْجابِيَةُ“ is the large basin. Al-Aʿshā said:
كَجابِيَةِ السِّيجِ العِراقِيِّ تَفْهَقُ
(Like the basin of the Iraqi [estate-]wall, brimming over.)
That is: they make for him his bowls like the great basins in which water is collected. ﴿وَقُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ﴾: fixed. ﴿اعْمَلُوا آلَ داوُدَ شُكْرًا﴾: ”شُكْرًا“ is accusative on two accounts. One of them: work for [the sake of] thanks, that is: thank Allah for what He has given you. And ”اِعْمَلُوا آلَ داوُدَ شُكْرًا“ may be on the meaning: give thanks with thanks.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿ما دَلَّهم عَلى مَوْتِهِ إلا دابَّةُ الأرْضِ تَأْكُلُ مِنسَأتَهُ﴾: ”اَلْمِنسَأةُ“ is the staff. It was only called ”مِنسَأةً“ because one drives with it (yunsaʾu bihā), and the meaning of ”يُنْسَأُ بِها“ is: one drives away with it and pushes back with it. When Solomon died, he died leaning on it — on his staff — and the jinn did not know of his death until the woodworm (al-araḍa) ate the staff and he fell down. ﴿فَلَمّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ الجِنُّ﴾ his death, ﴿أنْ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ الغَيْبَ ما لَبِثُوا في العَذابِ المُهِينِ﴾: the meaning is: "because had they known what was hidden from them, they would not have worked in subjection"; they only worked thinking that he was alive, overseeing their work. Some said: mankind perceived [the truth about] the jinn, that if they had known the unseen. It may also be that ”تَبَيَّنَتِ الجِنُّ أنْ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ الغَيْبَ“ means that the jinn perceived that they do not know the unseen; they used to give the impression that they knew the unseen, and they perceived that it had become clear to people that they do not know — just as you say to someone who claims something false before you, when you have made it clear to him: "I have shown that what he says is false", although he has always known that; but you wanted to rebuke him and let him know that you have learned the falseness of his claim.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَقَدْ كانَ لِسَبَإٍ في مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ﴾: it is also read: ”مَسْكِنِهِمْ“ — “with fatḥa and with kasra on the kāf —, and it is read: “ مَساكِنِهِمْ ”. It is also read: “ لِسَبَأ ” with fatḥa and without declension (tark al-ṣarf), and “ لِسَبَإٍ ”. Whoever reads fatḥa and leaves it undeclined does so because he makes “ سَبَأ ” the name of a tribe; and whoever declines it, with kasra and nunation, makes “ سَبَإٍ ” the name of the man and the name of the clan. All of it is permissible and good. ﴿آيَةٌ جَنَّتانِ﴾: “ آيَةٌ ” is nominative, the noun (ism) of “ كانَ ”; and “ جَنَّتانِ ” is nominative in two ways: as a badal (substitute) for “ آيَةٌ ”, and by an implied [subject], as though, when “ a sign ” was said, it was said: “ the sign is two gardens ”. “ اَلْجَنَّتانِ ” are the two orchards: they had two orchards, an orchard on the right and an orchard on the left. ﴿كُلُوا مِن رِزْقِ رَبِّكم واشْكُرُوا لَهُ﴾: the meaning is: “ it was said to them: eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him ”.
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ﴾ is on the meaning: “ this is a good land ”; ﴿وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾ is on the meaning: “ and Allah is a forgiving Lord ".

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿فَأعْرَضُوا﴾: the meaning is: they turned away from the command of Allah. ﴿فَأرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ العَرِمِ﴾: about ”اَلْعَرِمُ“ there are several views. Abū ʿUbayda said: “ [it is the] plural of “ عَرِمَةٌ ”, which is the dam and the embankment. It is said: “ اَلْعَرِمُ ” is the name of the valley. It is said: “ اَلْعَرِمُ ” here is the name of the rat that bored through the dam on them, which is what is called “ اَلْخُلْدُ ” (the mole-rat). And it is said: “ اَلْعَرِمُ ” is heavy rain. They were living in prosperity, and they had gardens on the right and on the left. A woman would go out with a basket on her head, working with her hands, and walk among those trees, and whatever she needed of the fruit of those trees would fall into her basket. But they were not grateful, so Allah sent a rat against them. They had a dam with gates in it, which they would open for whatever water they needed; that rat bored through it until it was breached upon them, and it flooded those two gardens. ﴿وَبَدَّلْناهم بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ﴾, that is: in place of these two gardens that were described, ﴿جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ﴾. And “ أُكْلٍ خَمْطٍ ”: ḍamma and sukūn on the kāf are both permissible; it is read: “ ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ ” and “ ذَواتَيْ أُكْلٍ خَمْطٍ ”. The meaning of “ خَمْطٍ ”: every plant that has taken on a bitter taste so that it cannot be eaten is called “ خَمْطٌ ”. In the book of al-Khalīl: “ اَلْخَمْطُ ” is the arāk tree. It has come in the exegesis that “ اَلْخَمْطُ ” is the arāk, and “ أُكُلُهُ " is its fruit; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 25]

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْناهم بِما كَفَرُوا﴾: ”ذَلِكَ“ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is: "We recompensed them with that for their disbelief". ﴿وَهَلْ نُجازِي إلا الكَفُورَ﴾: it is also read: ”وَهَلْ يُجازى“, and ”وَهَلْ يُجازِي إلّا الكَفُورَ“ is permissible. This is among the things that are asked about; it is said: " Allah, Mighty and Majestic, recompenses the ungrateful and the one who is not ungrateful. The meaning in this verse is that the believer has his evil deeds expiated, while the disbeliever has his deeds nullified and so is recompensed for every evil he does. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1], and He said: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا ما أسْخَطَ اللَّهَ وكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ فَأحْبَطَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 28]. So He, Majestic and Mighty, made known that He nullifies the deeds of the disbeliever, and He informed us that good deeds remove evil deeds, and that the believer's good deeds expiate his evil deeds.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهم وبَيْنَ القُرى الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها قُرًى ظاهِرَةً﴾: this is conjoined to His words: ﴿لَقَدْ كانَ لِسَبَإٍ في مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ جَنَّتانِ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 15] ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهم وبَيْنَ القُرى الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها قُرًى ظاهِرَةً﴾. So they had no need of provisions from the valley of Sabaʾ to Syria. It is said: the towns that We blessed are Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), and it is also said: Syria. So the towns from the valley of Sabaʾ to all these places were continuous.
﴿وَقَدَّرْنا فِيها السَّيْرَ﴾: We made their travel by measured stages; wherever they wanted to stay, they alighted at a town in safety.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿فَقالُوا رَبَّنا باعِدْ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا﴾: it is also read: ”رَبَّنا بَعِّدْ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“; it is read: ”رَبُّنا بَعَّدَ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“; it is read: ”رَبَّنا“ in the accusative, ”بَعُدَ بَيْنُ أسْفارِنا“ with ”بَيْنَ“ in the nominative; it is read: ”بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“; and it is read: ”رَبُّنا باعَدَ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“. ﴿وَظَلَمُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾. Whoever reads: ”بَعُدَ بَيْنُ أسْفارِنا“ with ”بَيْنَ“ in the nominative, the meaning is: "what connects with our journeying has become distant". Whoever reads: ”بَعُدَ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا“, the meaning is: "what is between our journeys has become distant", and "our travel between our journeys has become long". Whoever reads: ”باعِدْ“, it is by way of request, and the meaning is that they grew weary of ease and were ungrateful for the blessing, as the people of Moses said: ﴿فادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنا مِمّا تُنْبِتُ الأرْضُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 61], up to His words: ﴿الَّذِي هو أدْنى بِالَّذِي هو خَيْرٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 61]. ﴿وَمَزَّقْناهم كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾, that is: "We scattered them throughout the lands", because when Allah took away their two gardens and flooded their place, they dispersed throughout the lands, and the Arabs came to use them as a proverb for dispersal, saying: ”تَفَرَّقُوا أيْدِيَ سَبَإٍ“ and ”أيادِي سَبَإٍ“ (they scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ). The poet said:
مِن صادِرٍ أوْ وارِدٍ أيْدِي سَبا
(Of those departing or arriving, [scattered like] the hands of Sabaʾ.)
And Kuthayyir said:
أيادِي سَبا يا عَزُّ ما كُنْتُ بَعْدَكم ∗∗∗ فَلَمْ يَحْلُ لِلْعَيْنَيْنِ بِعْدَكِ مَنظَرُ
(Scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ, O ʿAzza, I have been since you [left]; no sight has been sweet to the eyes after you.)

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾: it is also read: ”وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ“, with ”إبْلِيسُ“ in the nominative and the ẓann in the accusative. His being true in his supposition is that he supposed of them that, when he led them astray, they would follow him, and he found them so; he said: ﴿فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لأُغْوِيَنَّهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [Ṣād: 82] ﴿إلا عِبادَكَ مِنهُمُ المُخْلَصِينَ﴾ [Ṣād: 83]. Whoever says ”صَدَّقَ“ makes the ẓann accusative because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and whoever lightens it, saying ”صَدَقَ“, makes the ẓann accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), on the meaning: "Iblīs was true about them in a supposition he supposed", and "he was true in his supposition". There are two other ways in it. One of them: ”وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنُّهُ“, ”ظَنُّهُ“ being a badal (substitute) for ”إبْلِيسُ“, as the Exalted said: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الحَرامِ قِتالٍ فِيهِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 217]. And it is permissible: ”وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنُّهُ“ «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the source, identical to the previous form; the meaning given suggests the reading ṣadaqa … ẓannu Iblīsa]», on the meaning: "the supposition of Iblīs proved true by their following him". Both have been read.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَما كانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن سُلْطانٍ﴾, that is: he had no proof (ḥujja) over them, as He said: ﴿إنَّ عِبادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 65]. ﴿إلا لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِالآخِرَةِ مِمَّنْ هو مِنها في شَكٍّ﴾, that is: except that We might know that with the knowledge of its occurring from them, and that is what they are recompensed for. Allah knows the unseen, and He knows who will believe from who will disbelieve before the believer believes and the disbeliever disbelieves; but that does not entail reward or punishment. They are rewarded and punished only for what they used to do.
His words: ﴿وَما لَهُ مِنهم مِن ظَهِيرٍ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 22]: He means that those whom they claim to be partners of Allah, of the angels and others, have no partnership, and there is no helper for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in what He created.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفاعَةُ عِنْدَهُ إلا لِمَن أذِنَ لَهُ﴾, with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the hamza. The meaning is: ”لِمَن أذِنَ لَهُ“, that is: "for the one whom Allah permits to intercede". It is also permissible [as]: "except for the one for whom He permits intercession to be made", so that ”مَن“ refers to the interceders, or it may refer to those interceded for. The better is that it refers to the interceders, because of His words: ﴿حَتّى إذا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, since those from whose hearts fear is removed here are the angels. It is also read: ”حَتّى إذا فَزَّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ“ with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and al-Ḥasan read: ”حَتّى إذا فُرِّغَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ“, with the undotted rāʾ and the dotted ghayn. The meaning of ”فُزِّعَ“ is: fear was removed from their hearts; and ”فَزَّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ“: Allah removed fear from their hearts. Al-Ḥasan's reading ”فُرِّغَ“ comes back to this meaning, because they were emptied of fear. The explanation of this is that when Gabriel — upon him be peace — descended to Muḥammad ﷺ with revelation, the angels thought that he had descended for something of the matter of the Hour, and they were terrified at that. When the fear was removed from them, ﴿قالُوا ماذا قالَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾, asking: "For what is Gabriel descending?" ﴿قالُوا الحَقَّ﴾, that is: they said: He said the truth. Had it been read: ”قالُوا الحَقُّ“, it would be a valid way, the meaning being: "they said: it is the truth".

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿وَإنّا أوْ إيّاكم لَعَلى هُدًى أوْ في ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: it is related in the exegesis that the meaning is: "We are surely upon guidance, and you are surely in manifest error". This is not permissible in the language, but in exegesis it comes back to this meaning: "We are upon guidance or in manifest error, or you are upon guidance or in manifest error". This is like when someone says — when the situation indicates that he is truthful —: "One of us is truthful and one of us is a liar", the meaning being: "one of us is truthful or a liar". The meaning of the verse comes back to: "We, because of the proof we have established, are upon guidance, and you are in manifest error".

zajjaj:26-26.t: His words: ﴿ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ بَيْنَنا بِالحَقِّ﴾: the meaning of ”يَفْتَحُ“ is: He judges; and likewise ”اَلْفَتّاحُ“ is the Judge.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ أرُونِيَ الَّذِينَ ألْحَقْتُمْ بِهِ شُرَكاءَ﴾: the meaning is: ”ألْحَقْتُمُوهم بِهِ“ (you joined them to Him), but [the pronoun] was omitted because it is in the ṣila (relative clause) of ”اَلَّذِينَ“.
His words: ﴿كَلا بَلْ هو اللَّهُ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾: the meaning of ”كَلّا“ is deterrence and alerting; the meaning is: "Desist from this saying and wake up from your misguidance; rather, He is Allah, the One, like whom there is nothing."

zajjaj:28-28.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْناكَ إلا كافَّةً لِلنّاسِ بَشِيرًا ونَذِيرًا﴾: the meaning of ”كافَّةً“ in the language is encompassing; the meaning is: “We sent you encompassing all people in warning and conveying. So Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ to the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and he said: «“ I am the forerunner of the Arabs to Islam, Ṣuhayb is the forerunner of the Byzantines, Bilāl is the forerunner of the Abyssinians, and Salmān is the forerunner of the Persians "», that is: the message is universal, and these are the forerunners from among the non-Arabs.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His words: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ بِهَذا القُرْآنِ ولا بِالَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾: they mean: "We do not believe in what Muḥammad ﷺ has brought, nor in the earlier scriptures."

zajjaj:33-33.t: His words: ﴿بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ﴾: its meaning is: "rather, your scheming by night and day". ﴿وَنَجْعَلَ لَهُ أنْدادًا﴾: likenesses. ﴿وَأسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ لَمّا رَأوُا العَذابَ﴾: “they concealed it among themselves; they turned to blaming one another and making one another aware of the remorse. ﴿إلا قالَ مُتْرَفُوها﴾ [Sabaʾ: 34]: “ مُتْرَفُوها " are those of luxury, and they are its chiefs and the leaders of evil, whom the lowly follow.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما أمْوالُكم ولا أوْلادُكم بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكم عِنْدَنا زُلْفى﴾: He did not say ”بِاللَّتَيْنِ“, nor ”بِاللَّذَيْنِ“, nor ”بِاللّاتِي“, and all of that would be permissible, but what is in the Muṣḥaf is ”اَلَّتِي“. The meaning is: "Your wealth is not that which brings you near, nor are your children those who bring you near", but [one of the two] was omitted for brevity and concision; we have explained the like of this.
His words: ﴿إلا مَن آمَنَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا﴾: the position of ”مَن“ is accusative by exception, as a badal (substitute) for the kāf and mīm, on the meaning: “nothing brings near except [for] whoever believes and does righteous deeds", that is: “ wealth brings near only whoever believes and uses it in obedience to Allah ”. ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ لَهم جَزاءُ الضِّعْفِ بِما عَمِلُوا﴾: “ اَلضِّعْفُ ” here needs explanation, and I know of no one who has explained it clearly. “ جَزاءُ الضِّعْفِ ” here is ten good deeds; its interpretation is: “ for those there is the recompense of the multiple whose measure We have made known to you ”, and that is His words: ﴿مَن جاءَ بِالحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أمْثالِها﴾ [al-Anʿām: 160]. There are several ways in it in Arabic. What has been read is the genitive of “ اَلضِّعْفِ ”, by annexing the recompense to it. It is permissible: “ فَأُولَئِكَ لَهم جَزاءٌ الضِّعْفُ ”, on the meaning: “ for those there is the multiple as a recompense ”, the meaning being: “ in the state of recompensing ”. It is permissible: “ فَأُولَئِكَ لَهم جَزاءً الضِّعْفَ ”, with “ اَلضِّعْفَ ” in the accusative, the meaning being: “ for those it is that We recompense them the multiple ”. The nominative of “ اَلضِّعْفُ ” is permissible on two accounts: on the meaning: “ for those there is the multiple ”, “ اَلضِّعْفُ ” being a badal (substitute) for the recompense; and it may be nominative with “ هو ” implied: “ for those there is a recompense ” — as though one asked: What is it? And He said: “ the multiple ”. The accusative in “ اَلضِّعْفِ ” is also permissible as the object of a verb whose agent is not named (i.e. passive), on the meaning: “ for those it is that they be recompensed the multiple ”. The reading, of all these ways, is the genitive of “ اَلضِّعْفِ ” and the nominative of “ جَزاءٌ ".

zajjaj:44-44.t: His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَما آتَيْناهم مِن كُتُبٍ يَدْرُسُونَها وما أرْسَلْنا إلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ مِن نَذِيرٍ﴾: by this are meant the Arab idolaters in Mecca; they were not people of scriptures, and no prophet was sent [to them] before Muḥammad ﷺ.

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿وَكَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ وما بَلَغُوا مِعْشارَ ما آتَيْناهُمْ﴾, that is: a tenth of the strength and power that We gave those before them. ﴿فَكَذَّبُوا رُسُلِي فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ﴾: the yāʾ was dropped; the meaning is: "So how was My reproach (nakīrī)?", because it is the end of a verse.

zajjaj:46-46.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما أعِظُكم بِواحِدَةٍ﴾, that is: I exhort you to affirm the oneness of Allah and to say: "There is no god but Allah", sincerely.
